title: Currency Overview
disambiguation: This chunk is about the Currencies mechanic itself, not its interactions. It is not about unrelated shop pages, UI formatting, or non-game currencies outside the Tower economy.
content: Currency Overview. The game economy is split between run-only currencies, permanent account currencies, and special-purpose progression currencies. Cash is a run-only economy, while most other currencies persist on the account and feed permanent progression systems. Different currencies are tied to different parent systems such as Tournaments, Events, Guilds, Labs, Modules, and the Workshop. Cash: Run-only currency used for temporary upgrades during a run. Persistence: run-only. Coins: Core progression currency used for Workshop, Labs, and permanent enhancement unlocks. Persistence: account. Gems: Core premium currency used for cards, slots, rushing, modules, and extra tournament entries. Persistence: account. Power Stones: Premium progression currency used to buy and upgrade Ultimate Weapons. Persistence: account. Medals: Event currency used for Event Shop purchases and saved between events. Persistence: account. Elite Cells: Elite-enemy currency used to buy lab boosts. Persistence: account. Keys: Legend-tournament currency used for Vault tech-tree upgrades. Persistence: account. Bits: Guild-shop currency used for guardian chip upgrades. Persistence: account. Tokens: Guild-shop currency earned from weekly challenge and guild reward systems. Persistence: account. Module Currency: Module Shards level modules, and Reroll Dice reroll module substats. Persistence: account.

title: Cash
disambiguation: This chunk is about the Cash mechanic itself, not its interactions. It is not about unrelated shop pages, UI formatting, or non-game currencies outside the Tower economy.
content: Cash. Cash is the temporary in-run currency used for buying upgrades during the active run. Enemy base-cash scaling: Wave 1-200: +1 cash every 10 waves; Wave 201+: +1 cash every 20 waves. Cash per Wave is a flat payout applied first at the end of each wave. Interest is then calculated as a percentage of current unspent cash on hand, up to the current interest cap. Because Cash per Wave is applied before Interest, end-of-wave cash can push the player into a higher interest payout when they were previously below cap. Cash flow improves through Cash Bonus, Cash / Wave, Interest / Wave, and Max Interest upgrades from Workshop and Labs. Cards that improve cash flow include Cash and Enemy Balance. Golden Tower, cash-oriented module effects, and Workshop Enhancements also increase run cash flow. Cash Bonus enhancement unlocks for free after completing the Workshop Enhancement labs. It increases the cash bonus multiplier by x1 when unlocked and by 0.01x per level. It also increases Cash / Wave, Interest / Wave, and Max Interest per wave by 1% each level. Its maximum level is 400 for a 5x bonus.

title: Coins
disambiguation: This chunk is about the Coins mechanic itself, not its interactions. It is not about unrelated shop pages, UI formatting, or non-game currencies outside the Tower economy.
content: Coins. Coins are the backbone progression currency for permanent upgrades. Coins come from enemy kills other than the pure-basic-only case, Coins / Wave, Daily Missions, and Milestones. Coin efficiency depends on both tier and wave depth, so higher tier is only better when the run still reaches strong spawn-rate and enemy-composition breakpoints. Coin flow improves through higher tiers, Coins / Kill, Coins / Wave, economy cards, Ultimate Weapon income tools, module effects, perks, guardian bounty effects, and Workshop Enhancements. Important Ultimate Weapon income contributors named in the source are Golden Tower, Black Hole Coin Bonus, Spotlight Coin Bonus, and Death Wave Coin Bonus. Coin Bonus enhancement requires 50 billion coins spent on Utility enhancements to unlock. It increases the Coin Bonus multiplier by x1 when unlocked and by 0.01x per level. Its maximum level is 200 for a 3x bonus. The source notes that Coin Bonus enhancement affects both tier bonus and Coins / Kill, which makes the overall benefit effectively squared.

title: Gems
disambiguation: This chunk is about the Gems mechanic itself, not its interactions. It is not about unrelated shop pages, UI formatting, or non-game currencies outside the Tower economy.
content: Gems. Gems are a core premium currency used for both permanent unlocks and speed/convenience spending. Floating gems spawn around the tower, up to ten per run, at two gems per pickup. Floating gems spawn about once every 400 to 500 waves and no more than once every 15 minutes. Ad gems appear about every 10 minutes and grant five gems per claim. Gems also come from store claims, tournaments, medal and guild exchange paths, daily missions, weekly reward systems, and real-money purchases. Gems are spent on cards, card slots, lab slots, rushing lab upgrades, modules, and tournament tickets. This makes Gems both a progression currency and a convenience currency rather than a single-purpose shop token.

title: Power Stones
disambiguation: This chunk is about the Power Stones mechanic itself, not its interactions. It is not about unrelated shop pages, UI formatting, or non-game currencies outside the Tower economy.
content: Power Stones. Power Stones buy and upgrade Ultimate Weapons. Purchases of 500 Power Stones or more show a confirmation prompt. Main sources listed are Tournaments, Event medal exchanges, weekly rewards, Milestones, and store offers.

title: Medals
disambiguation: This chunk is about the Medals mechanic itself, not its interactions. It is not about unrelated shop pages, UI formatting, or non-game currencies outside the Tower economy.
content: Medals. Medals are the Event Shop currency. They are obtained from Event Missions, Weekly Rewards from Daily Missions, and Guardian Fetch. Medals do not expire when an Event ends, so they can be saved for future Event Shops. Relic threshold progress only counts medals earned during the corresponding event, not carried-over medals or daily-mission box medals.

title: Elite Cells
disambiguation: This chunk is about the Elite Cells mechanic itself, not its interactions. It is not about unrelated shop pages, UI formatting, or non-game currencies outside the Tower economy.
content: Elite Cells. Elite Cells only come from defeating Vampire, Ray, and Scatter elites. For Tiers 1 through 13, each elite drops between 1 and X cells where X equals the current tier, for an average of (1 + X) / 2. Tier 14-21 base elite-cell rows: Tier 14: 7-14 cells, average 10.5, +50% from prior average; Tier 15: 11-15 cells, average 13, +23.8% from prior average; Tier 16: 12-16 cells, average 14, +7.69% from prior average; Tier 17: 12-17 cells, average 14.5, +3.57% from prior average; Tier 18: 12-18 cells, average 15, +3.45% from prior average; Tier 19: 15-19 cells, average 17, +13.3% from prior average; Tier 20: 15-20 cells, average 17.5, +2.94% from prior average; Tier 21: 15-21 cells, average 18, +2.86% from prior average. Elite Cell flow improves through Death Wave Cell Bonus, higher tiers, higher waves, Cells Bonus in Workshop Enhancements, and run-speed helpers such as Enemy Balance, Wave Skip, and Intro Sprint masteries. Cells / Kill Bonus enhancement requires 500 billion coins spent on Utility enhancements, starts at x1, increases by 0.01x per level, and caps at level 200 for a 3x bonus.

content: Keys. Keys are earned from placing 1st through 15th in Legend Tournament. They are used for unique Tower upgrades in the Vault tech trees.

content: Bits. Bits are bought from the Guild Shop using Guild Tokens and are used for guardian chip upgrades. The source lists Guild Chests at 10, 25, 50, and 100 bits for 185 bits per week. It also lists Guild Shop bit purchases at 25, 50, and 75 for 150 bits per month, with a stated combined monthly total of 890 bits.

disambiguation: This chunk is about the Tokens mechanic itself, not its interactions. It is not about unrelated shop pages, UI formatting, or non-game currencies outside the Tower economy.
content: Tokens. Tokens are earned from Weekly Challenge boxes and Guild Reward Chests. They are spent in the Guild Shop on items and seasonal currency purchases.

title: Module Currency
disambiguation: This chunk is about the Module Currency mechanic itself, not its interactions. It is not about unrelated shop pages, UI formatting, or non-game currencies outside the Tower economy.
content: Module Currency. Module Shards are used to upgrade module levels and can be earned from enemy drops and daily rewards. There are labs that increase module-shard drop rate. Reroll Dice are used to roll new module substats and apply across module types rather than being locked to one module family.

topic: Cash with Cash Bonus Enhancement and Golden Tower
title: Cash with Cash Bonus Enhancement and Golden Tower
disambiguation: This chunk is about the interaction between Cash, Cash Bonus Enhancement, and Golden Tower, not the individual mechanics. It is not about coin-only farming, unrelated utility stats, or generic run advice.
content: Cash with Cash Bonus Enhancement and Golden Tower. Cash Bonus Enhancement is not only a visible cash multiplier; it also raises Cash / Wave and Interest / Wave support values as part of the same upgrade path. Golden Tower then multiplies kill-based income during activation windows, making it one of the major temporary run-income spikes for cash flow. Taken together, permanent enhancement scaling and Ultimate Weapon income windows determine how quickly late-run cash can snowball.
interaction_summary: Cash flow is improved both by Workshop Enhancement support scaling and by Golden Tower activation windows, so run cash is shaped by permanent utility growth plus temporary income windows.

topic: Coins with Tier Coin Bonus, Theme Passive Coin Bonus, and Coin Bonus Enhancement
title: Coins with Tier Coin Bonus, Theme Passive Coin Bonus, and Coin Bonus Enhancement
disambiguation: This chunk is about the interaction between Coins, Tier Coin Bonus, Theme Passive Coin Bonus, and Coin Bonus Enhancement, not the individual mechanics. It is not about cash flow, event prices, or unrelated cosmetic effects.
content: Coins with Tier Coin Bonus, Theme Passive Coin Bonus, and Coin Bonus Enhancement. Tier Coin Bonus determines the base economy pressure-reward tradeoff for a run, while Theme Passive Coin Bonus adds additive category ownership value outside the run itself. Coin Bonus Enhancement further increases the coin economy and is called out in the source as effectively squared because it affects both tier bonus and Coins / Kill. That means coin efficiency is never one slider; it is the result of tier choice, owned passive multipliers, and permanent enhancement scaling working together.
interaction_summary: Coin farming is shaped by multiple permanent multipliers at once: tier selection, owned-theme bonus, and Coin Bonus Enhancement all stack into the long-term coin economy.

title: Gems with Tournaments and Labs
disambiguation: This chunk is about the interaction between Gems, Tournaments, and Labs, not the individual mechanics. It is not about module shards, event medals, or unrelated reset costs.
content: Gems with Tournaments and Labs. Tournament Rewards are one of the recurring non-store sources of Gems. On the spending side, Gems are heavily tied to Labs through lab-slot unlocks and Lab Rushing, which converts Gems directly into faster permanent progress. That source-and-sink pairing is why Gems sit at the center of both competitive rewards and long-term account acceleration.
interaction_summary: Tournaments are one recurring Gems source, while Labs are one of the biggest Gems sinks because Gems can rush research timers and buy additional lab capacity.

topic: Power Stones with Tournaments and Events
title: Power Stones with Tournaments and Events
disambiguation: This chunk is about the interaction between Power Stones, Tournaments, and Events, not the individual mechanics. It is not about gems, guild currencies, or unrelated upgrade menus.
content: Power Stones with Tournaments and Events. Tournament rewards are the main recurring Power Stone source and therefore the main progression driver for Ultimate Weapons. Events add a second route by letting medals be exchanged into stones through Event Shop currency purchases. That makes Power Stones a cross-system currency even though Tournaments remain the dominant source in normal progression.
interaction_summary: Power Stones mainly enter the account from Tournaments, but Events also provide an exchange path that turns medals into additional stone income.

topic: Medals with Events and Event Shop
title: Medals with Events and Event Shop
disambiguation: This chunk is about the interaction between Medals, Events, and Event Shop, not the individual mechanics. It is not about guild tokens, tournament keys, or unrelated reward ladders.
content: Medals with Events and Event Shop. Medals originate inside the Events system rather than as a free-standing global currency. The Event Shop is the sink that turns those medals into stones, gems, shards, themes, music, bots, and rerun relics. Because medals do not expire, Events determine income cadence while the Event Shop determines when that saved value is actually spent.
interaction_summary: Events generate Medals through missions and weekly reward sources, and Event Shop is the place where those Medals are converted into lasting account value.

topic: Elite Cells with Labs and Cells / Kill Bonus Enhancement
title: Elite Cells with Labs and Cells / Kill Bonus Enhancement
disambiguation: This chunk is about the interaction between Elite Cells, Labs, and Cells / Kill Bonus Enhancement, not the individual mechanics. It is not about gem rushing, ordinary coins, or unrelated workshop categories.
content: Elite Cells with Labs and Cells / Kill Bonus Enhancement. Lab Boosting is the primary Elite Cell sink and turns stored cells into temporary research-speed multipliers. Cells / Kill Bonus Enhancement raises elite-cell income on the farming side, which changes how quickly the player can sustain repeated lab boosts. This creates a direct loop between run farming efficiency and the lab-speed economy built on Elite Cells.
interaction_summary: Elite Cells are spent by Lab Boosting, and the Workshop cell enhancement increases how many cells a farming run can return before those boosts are purchased.

title: Bits and Tokens with Guilds
disambiguation: This chunk is about the interaction between Bits, Tokens, and Guilds, not the individual mechanics. It is not about event medals, tournament placements, or unrelated tracker state.
content: Bits and Tokens with Guilds. Tokens come from Weekly Challenge boxes and Guild Reward Chests and are then spent in the Guild Shop. Bits are part of that same guild economy, with the source text listing both chest-derived bits and seasonal Guild Shop bit purchases. In practice, Tokens are the routing currency for guild spending while Bits are one of the progression outputs that feed guardian chip upgrades.
interaction_summary: Tokens are the Guild Shop currency, while Bits are one of the resources obtained through guild reward and shop systems and then spent on guardian progression.

title: Daily Missions Overview
disambiguation: This chunk is about the Daily Missions mechanic itself, not its interactions. It is not about event missions, unrelated tracker reminders, or non-daily reward systems outside this mechanic.
content: Daily Missions Overview. Daily missions are progress based challenges given every 8 hours. Completion of daily challenges provide coins and gems. Completing enough daily missions will earn access to weekly rewards.

title: Daily Mission Challenge Pool
disambiguation: This chunk is about the Daily Mission Challenges mechanic itself, not its interactions. It is not about event missions, unrelated tracker reminders, or non-daily reward systems outside this mechanic.
content: Daily Mission Challenge Pool. Unlike events, daily missions are given based on player progress. Players only receive card and ultimate weapon challenges when they have the corresponding unlock. Players will have different challenges than each other and are able to complete all challenges received.

title: Daily Mission Rewards
disambiguation: This chunk is about the Daily Mission Rewards mechanic itself, not its interactions. It is not about event missions, unrelated tracker reminders, or non-daily reward systems outside this mechanic.
content: Daily Mission Rewards. Daily missions give 3 gems and a number of coins and shards based on the highest tier unlocked. The highest tier unlocked also impacts coins from weekly rewards and guild rewards. The amount of shards per mission can be increased with the Daily Mission Shards lab.

title: Daily Mission Tier Rewards
disambiguation: This chunk is about the Daily Mission Tier Rewards mechanic itself, not its interactions. It is not about event missions, unrelated tracker reminders, or non-daily reward systems outside this mechanic.
content: Daily Mission Tier Rewards. The base daily mission payout is 3 gems plus tier-scaled coins and shards. Tier reward table: Tier 1: 25 coins and N/A shards. Tier 2: 100 coins and 3 shards. Tier 3: 1000 coins and 5 shards. Tier 4: 10,000 coins and 8 shards. Tier 5: 25,000 coins and 12 shards. Tier 6: 80,000 coins and 15 shards. Tier 7: 250,000 coins and 20 shards. Tier 8: 500,000 coins and 25 shards. Tier 9: 1.00 Mil coins and 30 shards. Tier 10: 3.00 Mil coins and 34 shards. Tier 11: 5.00 Mil coins and 38 shards. Tier 12: 8.00 Mil coins and 42 shards. Tier 13: 15.00 Mil coins and 48 shards. Tier 14: 30.00 Mil coins and 55 shards. Tier 15: 75.00 Mil coins and 60 shards. Tier 16: 150.00 Mil coins and 65 shards. Tier 17: 300.00 Mil coins and 70 shards. Tier 18: 500 Mil coins and 75 shards. Tier 19: 750 Mil coins and 80 shards. Tier 20: 1.25 Bil coins and 85 shards. Tier 21: 2.00 Bil coins and 90 shards.

title: Daily Mission Weekly Rewards
disambiguation: This chunk is about the Weekly Mission Rewards mechanic itself, not its interactions. It is not about event missions, unrelated tracker reminders, or non-daily reward systems outside this mechanic.
content: Daily Mission Weekly Rewards. Weekly rewards are earned for every 5 daily missions completed until 35 missions complete, and the rewards can be re-earned each week. Weekly reward ladder: 5 missions gives coins x3, 10 gems, 0 medals, 0 stones, and 5 tokens. 10 missions gives coins x4, 15 gems, 10 medals, 0 stones, and 5 tokens. 15 missions gives coins x5, 20 gems, 15 medals, 0 stones, and 5 tokens. 20 missions gives coins x7, 25 gems, 20 medals, 0 stones, and 5 tokens. 25 missions gives coins x10, 30 gems, 25 medals, 10 stones, and 5 tokens. 30 missions gives coins x15, 35 gems, 30 medals, 15 stones, and 5 tokens. 35 missions gives coins x20, 50 gems, 35 medals, 20 stones, and 5 tokens. Weekly totals are coins x64, 185 gems, 135 medals, 45 stones, and 35 tokens.

title: Daily Mission Reroll Lab
disambiguation: This chunk is about the Reroll Daily Mission mechanic itself, not its interactions. It is not about event missions, unrelated tracker reminders, or non-daily reward systems outside this mechanic.
content: Daily Mission Reroll Lab. Reroll Daily Mission allows missions to be rerolled for 5 gems. A different mission will always be rolled. Reroll Daily Mission is unlocked at Tier 4 Wave 30. Reroll Daily Mission has 1 level. Lab levels: Level 1 takes 1d 15h 59m, costs 20,000,000 coins, and gives Unlocked.

topic: Daily Missions with Daily Mission Challenges
title: Daily Missions with Daily Mission Challenges
disambiguation: This chunk is about the interaction between Daily Missions and Daily Mission Challenges, not the individual mechanics. It is not about event missions, tournament tasks, or static quest lists that ignore account progress.
content: Daily Missions with Daily Mission Challenges. Daily Missions do not use one universal challenge list for every account. Instead, the Daily Mission Challenges are filtered by player progress, so card and ultimate weapon tasks only appear after those systems are unlocked. That makes the mission pool conditional on account progression rather than fixed across all players.
interaction_summary: Daily Mission Challenges are determined by account progress, so Daily Missions only serves challenge types the player has already unlocked.

title: Daily Mission Rewards with Tiers
disambiguation: This chunk is about the interaction between Daily Mission Rewards and Tiers, not the individual mechanics. It is not about event medals, milestone chests, or unrelated reward tables.
content: Daily Mission Rewards with Tiers. Daily Mission Rewards are not fixed across the whole game because the highest unlocked tier determines the coin and shard payout table. That same tier state also affects the coin value used for Weekly Mission Rewards and guild reward payouts. As a result, tier progression changes the value of both per-mission rewards and the related weekly reward economy.
interaction_summary: Daily Mission Rewards scale from the highest unlocked tier, and that tier state also determines the coin basis used for weekly and guild reward payouts.

topic: Daily Mission Rewards with Weekly Mission Rewards
title: Daily Mission Rewards with Weekly Mission Rewards
disambiguation: This chunk is about the interaction between Daily Mission Rewards and Weekly Mission Rewards, not the individual mechanics. It is not about unrelated event ladders, milestone chests, or non-daily payout systems.
content: Daily Mission Rewards with Weekly Mission Rewards. Daily Mission Rewards set the tier-based coin value earned from each completed mission. Weekly Mission Rewards then reuse that same tier coin basis through their x3 to x20 coin multipliers. That means the value of weekly coin payouts scales alongside the same tier progression that boosts individual mission rewards.
interaction_summary: Weekly Mission Rewards reuse the same tier-based coin basis as Daily Mission Rewards, so higher unlocked tiers raise both per-mission and weekly coin value.

title: Reroll Daily Mission with Tiers
disambiguation: This chunk is about the interaction between Reroll Daily Mission and Tiers, not the individual mechanics. It is not about event rerolls, mission reward scaling, or unrelated unlock menus.
content: Reroll Daily Mission with Tiers. Reroll Daily Mission is not available immediately when the Daily Missions system first appears. It unlocks only after the account reaches Tier 4 Wave 30. That means tier progression acts as the gate on when mission reroll control becomes available.
interaction_summary: Reroll Daily Mission is locked behind reaching Tier 4 Wave 30, so tier progression gates whether the reroll lab exists at all.

title: Enemies Overview and Categories
disambiguation: This chunk is about the Enemies mechanic itself, not its interactions. It is not about specific farming guides or tracker filters.
content: Enemies Overview and Categories. Enemy categories are Normal, Elite, Fleet, and Boss. Spawn caps at one time are 150 total: 120 normal, 20 elites, and 10 bosses. Fleet enemies use normal spawn-cap slots. Shared mechanics include a 4% damage heat-up per hit, 50% coin decay after more than 3 waves alive, and 4% mass growth for each wave an enemy survives.

title: Normal and Boss Enemy Rules
disambiguation: This chunk is about the Normal and Boss Enemies mechanic itself, not its interactions. It is not about elite-only or fleet-only behavior.
content: Normal and Boss Enemy Rules. Normal enemies include Basic, Fast, Ranged, Tank, and Protector, and their spawn percentages sum to 100% each wave. Protectors have special spawn limits and cooldown behavior with a limited concurrent count. Bosses spawn at 100% on boss waves, usually every 10 waves unless battle conditions change that cadence. Bosses are immune to orbs except boss orb hit lab effects, death ray, shockwave, and Black Hole, and they can drop module shards and reroll shards.

title: Elite Enemy Rules
disambiguation: This chunk is about the Elite Enemies mechanic itself, not its interactions. It is not about general enemy caps or fleet rewards.
content: Elite Enemy Rules. Elite enemies are Vampire, Ray, and Scatter. Elite spawn is limited to one per wave early and up to two at higher waves. The UI can show 33% when one elite is guaranteed plus a possible second, and 100% when two are guaranteed. Elites are immune to orbs, death ray, shockwave, and Black Hole. Elite enemies drop elite cells on defeat, and Scatter children do not count toward the elite on-screen cap.

title: Fleet Enemy Mechanics
disambiguation: This chunk is about the Fleet Enemies mechanic itself, not its interactions. It is not about the specific stats of each fleet type or their reward table.
content: Fleet Enemy Mechanics. Fleet enemies appear naturally at Tier 14 and above and at very high waves on lower tiers. Fleet enemies are immune to orbs, death ray, shockwave, knockback, Black Hole damage, and Black Hole pull. They have 90% thorns resistance, 50% resistance to several stun and slow effects, and cannot be targeted by Magnetic Hook or Plasma Cannon. On lower tiers they begin at wave 15000 on Tier 1 and arrive 250 waves earlier for each higher tier, then repeat every 100 waves after their first appearance.

title: Fleet Enemy Type Overview
disambiguation: This chunk is about the Fleet Enemy Types mechanic itself, not its interactions. It is not about the generic fleet rule set or spawn schedule.
content: Fleet Enemy Type Overview. Saboteur has 2x speed and 20x health and disables a random ultimate weapon when it hits the tower, although the wall can block that debuff behavior. Commander has 0.5x speed and 20x health and applies a 2x nearby enemy health aura. Overcharge has 1x speed and 20x health and fires a returning projectile that doubles damage with each later hit.

title: Fleet Enemy Reward Table
disambiguation: This chunk is about the Fleet Rewards mechanic itself, not its interactions. It is not about elite cells, boss drops, or module upgrade costs.
content: Fleet Enemy Reward Table. Fleet drops are 80% reroll shards and 20% module shards. Fleet reward table: Tier 14: 1080 reroll shards and 5 module shards per type. Tier 15: 1200 reroll shards and 6 module shards per type. Tier 16: 1350 reroll shards and 7 module shards per type. Tier 17: 1500 reroll shards and 8 module shards per type. Tier 18: 1650 reroll shards and 9 module shards per type. Tier 19: 1800 reroll shards and 10 module shards per type. Tier 20: 1950 reroll shards and 11 module shards per type. Tier 21: 2100 reroll shards and 12 module shards per type.

title: Fleet Spawn Timing Table
disambiguation: This chunk is about the Fleet Spawn Timing mechanic itself, not its interactions. It is not about what fleets do once spawned.
content: Fleet Spawn Timing Table. Fleet spawn timing: Tier 14: first wave 2495, every 1000 waves. Tier 15: first wave 1495, every 750 waves. Tier 16: first wave 995, every 500 waves. Tier 17: first wave 495, every 250 waves. Tier 18: first wave 95, every 100 waves. Tier 19: first wave 45, every 50 waves. Tier 20: first wave 5, every 10 waves. Tier 21: first wave 5, every 10 waves with 2 fleets.

title: Enemy Type Summaries
disambiguation: This chunk is about the Enemy Type Summaries mechanic itself, not its interactions. It is not about the deeper rule tables for boss cadence or fleet resistance.
content: Enemy Type Summaries. Enemy type summaries: Basic: baseline enemy with no special behavior. Fast: 2x basic speed and worth 2 base coins. Tank: 0.5x basic speed, 5x basic health, worth 4 base coins. Ranged: ranged attacker worth 2 base coins. Protector: aura blocks insta-kills and reduces nearby damage taken. Boss: 0.3x speed and 20x health versus basic baseline, appears on boss waves. Vampire: 2x basic health, drains 2% tower max health per second, suppresses regen effects. Ray: basic health, charges 30 seconds then fires for 2x basic enemy damage, immune to knockback. Scatter: 2x basic health and repeatedly splits with halved health. Saboteur: 20x basic health and disables a random ultimate weapon on tower impact. Commander: 20x basic health and buffs nearby enemies. Overcharge: 20x basic health and uses escalating projectile damage behavior.

title: Enemy Lab Notes
disambiguation: This chunk is about the Enemy Labs mechanic itself, not its interactions. It is not about direct spawn rules or stat tables.
content: Enemy Lab Notes. Common, Fast, Tank, Ranged, Boss, and Protector enemy labs can alter the baseline assumptions behind simple x-multiplier comparisons. Elite-related labs include Vampire attack and health reductions, Ray attack and health reductions, Scatter attack and health reductions, Garlic Thorns, and Lightning Amplifier interactions with Scatter.

title: Elite Enemies with Elite Cells
disambiguation: This chunk is about the interaction between Elite Enemies and Elite Cells, not the individual mechanics. It is not about fleet rewards, gems, or unrelated lab timers.
content: Elite Enemies with Elite Cells. Elite Enemies are the enemies that drop Elite Cells when defeated. Because Elite Cells are tied to those Vampire, Ray, and Scatter kills, elite spawn behavior and kill consistency directly control the lab-boosting currency flow. That makes Elite Enemies the combat source layer behind the Elite Cells economy.
interaction_summary: Elite Enemies are the live combat source for Elite Cells, so elite spawn behavior directly determines elite-cell income.

title: Fleet Rewards with Module Currency
disambiguation: This chunk is about the interaction between Fleet Rewards and Module Currency, not the individual mechanics. It is not about elite cells, tournament prizes, or unrelated reroll advice.
content: Fleet Rewards with Module Currency. Fleet Rewards pay out reroll shards and module shards, which are the two parts of Module Currency. That means Fleet Rewards feed module progression directly instead of only acting as a generic loot table. In practice, fleets are one of the high-tier enemy systems that convert combat progression into Module Currency growth.
interaction_summary: Fleet Rewards are one of the enemy-side sources of Module Currency because fleets drop reroll shards and module shards directly.

title: Fleet Spawn Timing with Tiers
disambiguation: This chunk is about the interaction between Fleet Spawn Timing and Tiers, not the individual mechanics. It is not about battle-condition formulas, milestone unlocks, or unrelated reward systems.
content: Fleet Spawn Timing with Tiers. Fleet Spawn Timing is not fixed across all Tiers. Higher Tiers move the first fleet wave much earlier and shorten the repeat interval, which is why fleets become a much larger part of the run profile in late-tier play. That makes Tiers the system that controls how quickly Fleet Spawn Timing starts affecting combat and farming expectations.
interaction_summary: Fleet Spawn Timing scales by Tiers, with higher tiers introducing fleets earlier and repeating them more often.

title: Events Overview
disambiguation: This chunk is about the Events mechanic itself, not its interactions. It is not about unrelated tracker state, implementation details, or other game systems.
content: Events Overview. This file reorganizes event knowledge into the same keyed mechanic format used by other deterministic knowledge sources. The original raw source remains preserved in public/knowledge/events for side-by-side comparison. Definition: Events are repeating challenge cycles that reward medals for completing mission tiers. Type: System. Domain: Limited-Time Progression. Section: Events. Category: Progression. Behavior: Events unlock in Milestones at Tier 1 Wave 70. Events run on a repeating two-week cadence. Event progress centers on missions, medal rewards, relic thresholds, and the event shop.

title: Event Cycle
disambiguation: This chunk is about the Event Cycle mechanic itself, not its interactions. It is not about unrelated tracker state, implementation details, or other game systems.
content: Event Cycle. Definition: Event Cycle is the repeating two-week schedule that controls mission rollout and event downtime. Type: Schedule Rule. Domain: Events. Section: Events. Category: Schedule. Aliases: event rotation; event cadence. Behavior: Each event lasts 2 weeks. The first 8 days add new missions. The final 6 days add no new missions. When one event ends, the next event starts immediately.

title: Event Missions
disambiguation: This chunk is about the Event Missions mechanic itself, not its interactions. It is not about unrelated tracker state, implementation details, or other game systems.
content: Event Missions. Definition: Event Missions are the challenge list that awards medals during an event. Type: Objective System. Domain: Events. Section: Events. Category: Missions. Aliases: missions; event quests. Behavior: All event missions have 3 tiers. Higher tiers ask for larger requirements and give larger medal payouts. Missions remain available until the current event ends. Mission categories can draw from always-available tasks, base combat goals, workshop actions, cards, labs, and ultimate weapons.

title: Event Mission Tiers
disambiguation: This chunk is about the Event Mission Tiers mechanic itself, not its interactions. It is not about unrelated tracker state, implementation details, or other game systems.
content: Event Mission Tiers. Definition: Event Mission Tiers are the three medal-paying completion levels attached to each event mission. Type: Reward Table. Domain: Events. Section: Events. Category: Missions. Aliases: mission tier rewards. Behavior: Tier 1 rewards 10 medals. Tier 2 rewards 15 medals. Tier 3 rewards 20 medals. Each higher tier requires more progress than the previous tier.

title: Event Mission Rollout
disambiguation: This chunk is about the Event Mission Rollout mechanic itself, not its interactions. It is not about unrelated tracker state, implementation details, or other game systems.
content: Event Mission Rollout. Definition: Event Mission Rollout controls how many new missions appear during the first part of an event. Type: Availability Rule. Domain: Events. Section: Events. Category: Missions. Aliases: mission unlock schedule. Behavior: 7 missions are available on the first day. 2 more missions are added each day for the next 7 days. No new missions appear during the final 6 days of the event.

title: Event Rewards
disambiguation: This chunk is about the Event Rewards mechanic itself, not its interactions. It is not about unrelated tracker state, implementation details, or other game systems.
content: Event Rewards. Definition: Event Rewards are the medals and relic-threshold progress earned by completing event missions. Type: Reward System. Domain: Events. Section: Events. Category: Rewards. Aliases: medal rewards. Behavior: Completing mission tiers awards medals. Collected medals also count toward event relic thresholds when those medals were earned during the current event. Medals do not need to be spent to claim earned relic thresholds.

title: Event Booster
disambiguation: This chunk is about the Event Booster mechanic itself, not its interactions. It is not about unrelated tracker state, implementation details, or other game systems.
content: Event Booster. Definition: Event Booster doubles medal rewards for the event in which it is purchased. Type: Premium Modifier. Domain: Events. Section: Events. Category: Rewards. Aliases: booster; event pass booster. Behavior: The event booster doubles medal amounts for that event only. Booster-doubled medals also count toward relic thresholds. A booster must be purchased separately for each event where doubled medals are wanted.

title: Event Relic Progress
disambiguation: This chunk is about the Event Relic Progress mechanic itself, not its interactions. It is not about unrelated tracker state, implementation details, or other game systems.
content: Event Relic Progress. Definition: Event Relic Progress is the medal-earned threshold track that unlocks event relic rewards. Type: Threshold System. Domain: Events. Section: Events. Category: Rewards. Aliases: relic thresholds; event relic milestones. Behavior: 350 medals unlock the first rare relic. 550 medals unlock the first premium rare relic. 700 medals unlock the second epic relic. 1100 medals unlock the second premium epic relic. Medals carried over from previous events or earned from daily mission boxes do not count toward this progress.

title: Event Shop
disambiguation: This chunk is about the Event Shop mechanic itself, not its interactions. It is not about unrelated tracker state, implementation details, or other game systems.
content: Event Shop. Definition: Event Shop is the medal-spending store that remains available even when no event is active. Type: Store. Domain: Event Store. Section: Events. Category: Purchases. Aliases: event store. Behavior: The event shop spends medals. The shop remains open even while no event is running. The shop offers currencies, themes, relics, songs, and bots.

title: Event Shop Currency Purchases
disambiguation: This chunk is about the Event Shop Currency Purchases mechanic itself, not its interactions. It is not about unrelated tracker state, implementation details, or other game systems.
content: Event Shop Currency Purchases. Definition: Event Shop Currency Purchases are the medal exchange options and scaling price ladder for currencies in the event shop. Type: Cost Ladder. Domain: Medals. Section: Events. Category: Purchases. Aliases: event exchange; event currency costs. Behavior: Each exchange gives either 150 gems, 15 stones, or 250 shards. There are four shard types tied to the four module families. Buying shards increases the cost of the other shard types as well. Costs: Purchase 1 costs 40 medals. Purchase 2 costs 65 medals. Purchase 3 costs 90 medals. Purchase 4 costs 130 medals. Purchase 5 costs 175 medals. Purchase 6 costs 230 medals. Purchase 7 costs 380 medals.

title: Event Themes
disambiguation: This chunk is about the Event Themes mechanic itself, not its interactions. It is not about unrelated tracker state, implementation details, or other game systems.
content: Event Themes. Definition: Event Themes are rotating event-shop cosmetics that remain permanently unlocked once purchased. Type: Cosmetic Rotation. Domain: Event Store. Section: Events. Category: Purchases. Aliases: event themes. Behavior: Themes rotate each event and can be missed. One tower theme costs 150 medals. One background theme costs 250 medals. Purchased event themes remain available forever.

title: Event Relics
disambiguation: This chunk is about the Event Relics mechanic itself, not its interactions. It is not about unrelated tracker state, implementation details, or other game systems.
content: Event Relics. Definition: Event Relics are limited medal purchases sold in the event shop and distinct from the relics earned through medal thresholds. Type: Limited Purchase. Domain: Event Store. Section: Events. Category: Purchases. Aliases: event store relics. Behavior: Event-shop relics are sold at 200-medal and 500-medal price points. These relics can be limited to the sponsoring event. Earned event relics and purchased event relics are separate acquisition paths.

title: Event Songs
disambiguation: This chunk is about the Event Songs mechanic itself, not its interactions. It is not about unrelated tracker state, implementation details, or other game systems.
content: Event Songs. Definition: Event Songs are fixed event-shop purchases that each grant a permanent coin bonus. Type: Permanent Purchase. Domain: Event Store. Section: Events. Category: Purchases. Aliases: songs. Behavior: There are 3 songs available. Songs do not rotate. Each song costs 200 medals. Each song grants a +0.6% coin bonus.

title: Event Store Bots
disambiguation: This chunk is about the Event Store Bots mechanic itself, not its interactions. It is not about unrelated tracker state, implementation details, or other game systems.
content: Event Store Bots. Definition: Event Store Bots are the bot unlocks sold through the event shop for medals. Type: Store Category. Domain: Event Store. Section: Events. Category: Purchases. Aliases: bot shop; event bots. Behavior: Bots are purchased only with medals in the event shop. The shop offers Flame, Thunder, Golden, and Amplify bots. Purchased bots do not reset between events. Bots can be toggled on or off in the shop between rounds.

title: Event Bot Unlock Costs
disambiguation: This chunk is about the Event Bot Unlock Costs mechanic itself, not its interactions. It is not about unrelated tracker state, implementation details, or other game systems.
content: Event Bot Unlock Costs. Definition: Event Bot Unlock Costs are the escalating medal costs for unlocking additional bots from the event shop. Type: Cost Ladder. Domain: Medals. Section: Events. Category: Purchases. Aliases: bot unlock ladder. Behavior: The first bot costs 150 medals. The second bot costs 300 medals. The third bot costs 600 medals. The fourth bot costs 900 medals. Each additional unlocked bot raises the cost of the next bot unlock.

title: Bot Respec
disambiguation: This chunk is about the Bot Respec mechanic itself, not its interactions. It is not about unrelated tracker state, implementation details, or other game systems.
content: Bot Respec. Definition: Bot Respec refunds medal-based bot unlocks and medal-based bot upgrades for a gem fee once per event. Type: Reset Rule. Domain: Event Store. Section: Events. Category: Purchases. Aliases: event bot respec. Behavior: Bot respec costs 300 gems. Bot respec is available once per event. Bot labs are not refunded by bot respec. Only medal-related bot unlocks and medal-related bot upgrades are refunded.

title: Events with Milestones
disambiguation: This chunk is about the interaction between Events and Milestones, not the individual mechanics. It is not about mission rewards, bot upgrade values, or unrelated unlock systems.
content: Events with Milestones. Events do not exist for a run until the Milestones unlock at Tier 1 Wave 70 has been reached. That makes Milestones the gate that turns on the entire Events system, including missions, medal rewards, relic thresholds, and the event shop.
interaction_summary: Milestones gate when Events become available by unlocking the system at Tier 1 Wave 70.

topic: Event Cycle with Event Missions and Event Mission Rollout
title: Event Cycle with Event Missions and Event Mission Rollout
disambiguation: This chunk is about the interaction between Event Cycle, Event Missions, and Event Mission Rollout, not the individual mechanics. It is not about medal thresholds, bot respec, or unrelated schedules.
content: Event Cycle with Event Missions and Event Mission Rollout. Event Missions are only meaningful inside the active Event Cycle window. During that cycle, Event Mission Rollout starts with seven missions on day one and then adds two more missions per day for the next seven days. The final six days keep the same Event Missions list without adding new missions, so Event Cycle timing controls how much mission inventory is available at any given point.
interaction_summary: Event Cycle determines when Event Missions are active, and Event Mission Rollout decides how many of those missions appear across the first eight days.

topic: Event Rewards with Event Booster and Event Relic Progress
title: Event Rewards with Event Booster and Event Relic Progress
disambiguation: This chunk is about the interaction between Event Rewards, Event Booster, and Event Relic Progress, not the individual mechanics. It is not about shop purchases, bot stat lines, or unrelated premium systems.
content: Event Rewards with Event Booster and Event Relic Progress. Event Rewards are the medal payouts earned from completing mission tiers. If Event Booster is active, those earned medals are doubled for that event instead of staying at the base tier values. Those current-event earned medals then push Event Relic Progress toward the 350, 550, 700, and 1100 medal thresholds, while carried-over medals and daily mission box medals do not count for that threshold track.
interaction_summary: Event Rewards generate the medals, Event Booster doubles those medals for the active event, and both feed the current-event thresholds used by Event Relic Progress.

topic: Event Shop with Event Shop Currency Purchases and Medals
title: Event Shop with Event Shop Currency Purchases and Medals
disambiguation: This chunk is about the interaction between Event Shop, Event Shop Currency Purchases, and Medals, not the individual mechanics. It is not about relic threshold progress, bot cooldown stats, or unrelated currencies.
content: Event Shop with Event Shop Currency Purchases and Medals. The Event Shop is the place where Medals are spent rather than merely accumulated for thresholds. Event Shop Currency Purchases define the actual exchange outputs such as 150 gems, 15 stones, or 250 shards together with the rising medal-cost ladder. Because shard purchases increase costs across shard types, the value of Medals inside the Event Shop changes as more Event Shop Currency Purchases are made during the current event cycle.
interaction_summary: Event Shop spends Medals, and Event Shop Currency Purchases define the exchange outputs and escalating medal costs for those currency buys.

topic: Event Shop with Event Themes, Event Relics, and Event Songs
title: Event Shop with Event Themes, Event Relics, and Event Songs
disambiguation: This chunk is about the interaction between Event Shop, Event Themes, Event Relics, and Event Songs, not the individual mechanics. It is not about bot unlock costs, mission tiers, or unrelated cosmetic systems.
content: Event Shop with Event Themes, Event Relics, and Event Songs. Event Themes, Event Relics, and Event Songs are all medal sinks inside the Event Shop rather than threshold rewards from Event Relic Progress. Event Themes rotate by event and remain permanently available once purchased, Event Relics can be limited to the sponsoring event, and Event Songs stay non-rotating with a fixed coin-bonus role. That means the Event Shop is the shared parent system, while each of those three purchase categories applies its own permanence and rotation rules to how medals are converted into long-term account value.
interaction_summary: Event Shop is the store layer that sells Event Themes, Event Relics, and Event Songs for medals, with each category following its own availability and permanence rules.

topic: Event Store Bots with Bots and Medals
title: Event Store Bots with Bots and Medals
disambiguation: This chunk is about the interaction between Event Store Bots, Bots, and Medals, not the individual mechanics. It is not about per-bot stat breakpoints, relic progress thresholds, or unrelated stores.
content: Event Store Bots with Bots and Medals. Event Store Bots is the event-shop category that sells the permanent bot roster: Flame Bot, Thunder Bot, Golden Bot, Amplify Bot. Medals are the resource consumed to unlock those bots from the event store. Once unlocked, the purchased bot moves into the Bots progression system instead of resetting away with the current event.
interaction_summary: Event Store Bots is the medal-purchase path, while Bots is the actual permanent progression system those purchases unlock.

topic: Event Store Bots with Event Bot Unlock Costs
title: Event Store Bots with Event Bot Unlock Costs
disambiguation: This chunk is about the interaction between Event Store Bots and Event Bot Unlock Costs, not the individual mechanics. It is not about upgrade-medal costs after unlock, relic shop pricing, or unrelated trackers.
content: Event Store Bots with Event Bot Unlock Costs. Event Store Bots is not priced with a flat unlock fee for every bot. Instead, Event Bot Unlock Costs climbs from 150 to 300 to 600 to 900 medals as more bot unlocks are purchased. That makes the order of bot unlocks matter because each new Event Store Bots purchase permanently raises the medal cost of the next unlock.
interaction_summary: Event Store Bots uses Event Bot Unlock Costs to scale each new bot unlock higher than the previous one.

topic: Bot Respec with Event Store Bots and Gems
title: Bot Respec with Event Store Bots and Gems
disambiguation: This chunk is about the interaction between Bot Respec, Event Store Bots, and Gems, not the individual mechanics. It is not about mission payouts, event booster value, or unrelated refund systems.
content: Bot Respec with Event Store Bots and Gems. Bot Respec is the reset path for the permanent bot progression that originally came from Event Store Bots purchases. The reset costs 300 Gems and is limited to once per event. Only medal-based unlocks and medal-based bot upgrades are refunded, while bot labs remain outside the Bot Respec refund path.
interaction_summary: Bot Respec spends Gems once per event to refund medal-based Event Store Bots unlocks and medal-based upgrades without refunding bot labs.

title: Footguns Overview
disambiguation: This chunk is about the Footguns mechanic itself, not its interactions. It is not about general play efficiency, temporary resource mistakes, or unrelated tracker state outside this warning context.
content: Footguns Overview. Footguns are upgrades that can set an account behind and may take months to years to correct if they can be corrected at all. In the current state of the game, most footguns lower maximum potential but do not completely remove the ability to compete with other accounts.

title: What Is Not a Footgun
disambiguation: This chunk is about the Footgun Non-Examples mechanic itself, not its interactions. It is not about general play efficiency, temporary resource mistakes, or unrelated tracker state outside this warning context.
content: What Is Not a Footgun. Footguns are not just any inefficient choice or temporary resource mistake. The source specifically excludes waiting to unlock 5 labs, failing to do tournaments and missing stones, or unlocking Wall early and needing to respec.

title: Ultimate Weapon Footguns Overview
disambiguation: This chunk is about the Ultimate Weapon Footguns mechanic itself, not its interactions. It is not about general play efficiency, temporary resource mistakes, or unrelated tracker state outside this warning context.
content: Ultimate Weapon Footguns Overview. Ultimate Weapon picks are permanent even though all Ultimate Weapons can eventually be unlocked. Ultimate Weapon upgrades are also permanent and cannot be undone, so cooldown and pick mistakes have unusually long recovery windows.

title: Choosing an Ultimate Weapon Footgun
disambiguation: This chunk is about the Choosing an Ultimate Weapon mechanic itself, not its interactions. It is not about general play efficiency, temporary resource mistakes, or unrelated tracker state outside this warning context.
content: Choosing an Ultimate Weapon Footgun. Choosing the wrong Ultimate Weapon early is a long-term progression footgun because picks are permanent and later picks cost more. Why: Choosing Ultimate Weapons cannot be reversed, and picking new Ultimate Weapons gets more expensive. Taking some Ultimate Weapons early when there are better choices can set an account further behind. Solution: This can be corrected by unlocking more Ultimate Weapons, but that becomes an expensive process. To avoid this footgun, use the Ultimate Weapon guide before locking a pick.

title: Black Hole Cooldown Footgun
disambiguation: This chunk is about the Black Hole Cooldown mechanic itself, not its interactions. It is not about general play efficiency, temporary resource mistakes, or unrelated tracker state outside this warning context.
content: Black Hole Cooldown Footgun. Lowering Black Hole cooldown before Golden Tower is naturally synced can make 1:1 sync materially more expensive. Why: Black Hole cooldown can be harmful to upgrade without Golden Tower in sync. By lowering cooldown, it becomes more expensive to get Golden Tower to a 1:1 sync ratio. Solution: Black Hole cooldown will eventually self-correct because either enough stones are spent to match Golden Tower at 1:1 or Black Hole reaches max cooldown and settles into its best sync with max Golden Tower cooldown at 2:1.

topic: Changing the Cooldown of any Ultimate Weapon
title: Ultimate Weapon Cooldown Changes Footgun
disambiguation: This chunk is about the Changing the Cooldown of any Ultimate Weapon mechanic itself, not its interactions. It is not about general play efficiency, temporary resource mistakes, or unrelated tracker state outside this warning context.
data_source: FOOTGUN_ENTRIES["Changing the Cooldown of any Ultimate Weapon"]
content: Ultimate Weapon Cooldown Changes Footgun. Cooldown edits on any Ultimate Weapon can quietly lock an account out of sync-dependent strategies even when the pairing is not obvious at first glance. Why: Many strategies require Ultimate Weapons to be synced even if the pair does not seem obvious. The source example is a version of devo that uses Smart Missiles timing to weaken enemies and extend them, so the required cooldown relationship is strategic rather than cosmetic. Solution: Check what strategies exist and what syncs are needed before upgrading cooldowns. Some strategies do not require 1:1 syncs, but many still rely on exact breakpoints and missing them can lock the account out of those plans.
mechanics: Changing the Cooldown of any Ultimate Weapon

title: Natural GT/BH Sync Footgun
disambiguation: This chunk is about the Natural GT/BH Sync mechanic itself, not its interactions. It is not about general play efficiency, temporary resource mistakes, or unrelated tracker state outside this warning context.
content: Natural GT/BH Sync Footgun. Delaying natural Golden Tower and Black Hole sync is a footgun because MVN does not fully replace natural sync and still taxes uptime until much later progression. Why: The source warns that many players underestimate how much more value each Golden Tower activation gains once natural Golden Tower and Black Hole sync is reached. Multiverse Nexus is described as training wheels rather than a permanent excuse to ignore natural sync because it still adds average cooldown seconds until very high rarity and later long-term setups. Solution: Even while using Multiverse Nexus during the pursuit of Golden Tower and Black Hole sync, continue dropping stones so the account reaches at least 3:20 natural sync. The source treats that breakpoint as a long-run correction path the player will thank themselves for later. Current site module data for Multiverse Nexus shows average cooldown offsets of Epic +20s, Legendary +10s, Mythic +1s, Ancestral -10s.

title: Lab Footguns Overview
disambiguation: This chunk is about the Lab Footguns mechanic itself, not its interactions. It is not about general play efficiency, temporary resource mistakes, or unrelated tracker state outside this warning context.
content: Lab Footguns Overview. Lab upgrades are permanent and cannot normally be turned off once acquired. The source only calls out a small number of labs where more progress can be worse than fewer upgrades, with Range as the lone exception to the general permanence warning.

title: Bot Cooldown Footgun
disambiguation: This chunk is about the Bot Cooldowns mechanic itself, not its interactions. It is not about general play efficiency, temporary resource mistakes, or unrelated tracker state outside this warning context.
content: Bot Cooldown Footgun. Bot cooldown labs are a footgun because medal cooldowns can be respecced but lab cooldowns cannot, so bad sync breakpoints are expensive to undo. Why: Bot medal upgrades can be respecced, but labs cannot. That makes it expensive and difficult to resync bots to Ultimate Weapons or even to each other later on. The source especially calls out Golden Bot sync importance; current site data labels that bot as Coin Bot. To avoid: Get 6 medal and 2 lab cooldown upgrades to reach 100 seconds. After that, move in 5-second intervals with 1 medal plus 2 labs or 10-second intervals with 3 medals plus 1 lab until the bot reaches half of the Golden Tower and Death Wave sync cooldown. This preserves a 2:1 sync to Ultimate Weapon cooldown targets that are multiples of 10 seconds, and troublesome bots can simply be turned off in the medals menu. Solution: Eventually at max cooldowns all bots except Flame Bot, plus Black Hole and Death Wave, settle at 50 seconds while Golden Tower lands at 100 seconds. The source also notes a tech tree Bot Cooldown Slider upgrade for more precise syncing later. Current site bot data for the non-Flame sync bots is Thunder Bot base 120s, medal floor 75s, lab reduction -25s, final 100s; Golden Bot base 120s, medal floor 75s, lab reduction -25s, final 100s; Amplify Bot base 120s, medal floor 75s, lab reduction -25s, final 100s.

title: Chrono Field Range Footgun
disambiguation: This chunk is about the Chrono Field Range mechanic itself, not its interactions. It is not about general play efficiency, temporary resource mistakes, or unrelated tracker state outside this warning context.
content: Chrono Field Range Footgun. Chrono Field Range is a contextual footgun because extra zoom-out can lower coins per hour in some farms even though the lab is usually still worth maxing for tournament value. Why: Chrono Field Range zooms out the screen, which causes enemies to spawn further from the tower and take longer to be killed. The source warns that this lowers coins per hour. Solution: The same source also says the coins-per-hour loss is usually minimal and often outweighed by tournament benefits, so the practical recommendation is still to max the lab despite the downside. Current milestone data places Chrono Field Range at Tier 7 wave 90, which reinforces that the warning shows up late enough to matter mainly for developed farming and tournament setups rather than opening progression.

topic: Black Hole Cooldown with Golden Tower
title: Black Hole Cooldown with Golden Tower
disambiguation: This chunk is about the interaction between the Black Hole Cooldown footgun, Black Hole, and Golden Tower, not the individual mechanics. It is not a general farming guide or a generic cooldown table.
content: Black Hole Cooldown with Golden Tower. The Black Hole Cooldown footgun exists because Black Hole and Golden Tower are one of the key economy sync pairs in the game. When Black Hole cooldown is lowered ahead of plan, the account has to spend more to bring Golden Tower back to the desired overlap breakpoint instead of inheriting that ratio naturally. That makes the mistake reversible in theory, but expensive enough that the source still treats it as a long-term account setback rather than a harmless temporary detour.
interaction_summary: Lowering Black Hole cooldown before natural Golden Tower sync changes the stone path needed to reach the long-term GT/BH overlap targets.

topic: Ultimate Weapon Cooldown Changes with Smart Missiles, Golden Tower, and Black Hole
title: Ultimate Weapon Cooldown Changes with Smart Missiles, Golden Tower, and Black Hole
disambiguation: This chunk is about the interaction between the Ultimate Weapon cooldown-change footgun and sync-sensitive Ultimate Weapons, not the individual mechanics. It is not a tier list or a one-size-fits-all build order.
data_source: FOOTGUN_ENTRIES["Changing the Cooldown of any Ultimate Weapon"]
content: Ultimate Weapon Cooldown Changes with Smart Missiles, Golden Tower, and Black Hole. Changing the Cooldown of any Ultimate Weapon is broader than Black Hole and Golden Tower alone. The source example uses Smart Missiles timing inside a devo variant, which shows that even a weapon that does not look like a primary economy pair can still require exact sync timing to keep a strategy valid. Because of that, cooldown upgrades should be checked against strategy requirements first and not treated as isolated linear progression choices.
mechanics: Changing the Cooldown of any Ultimate Weapon
interaction_summary: Cooldown edits on one Ultimate Weapon can matter to broader strategy sync plans because Ultimate Weapon pairings are often functional rather than obvious from the UI alone.

topic: Natural GT/BH Sync with Multiverse Nexus, Golden Tower, Black Hole, and Death Wave
title: Natural GT/BH Sync with Multiverse Nexus, Golden Tower, Black Hole, and Death Wave
disambiguation: This chunk is about the interaction between the Natural GT/BH Sync footgun, Multiverse Nexus, and the affected Ultimate Weapons, not the individual mechanics. It is not a module rarity tier list or a generic uptime explainer.
content: Natural GT/BH Sync with Multiverse Nexus, Golden Tower, Black Hole, and Death Wave. The source treats Multiverse Nexus as a temporary sync aid rather than a permanent excuse to ignore natural Golden Tower and Black Hole sync. Current site module data reinforces that point because MVN still modifies the average cooldown by +20 seconds at Epic, +10 at Legendary, +1 at Mythic, and only reaches -10 at Ancestral. That means natural sync remains the durable long-run target even for accounts using MVN as a bridge while Golden Tower, Black Hole, and sometimes Death Wave are still being aligned.
interaction_summary: Multiverse Nexus forces shared activation timing, but its average-cooldown offsets mean it does not replace the long-term value of natural Golden Tower and Black Hole sync.

topic: Bot Cooldowns with Bots, Golden Tower, Death Wave, and Vault
title: Bot Cooldowns with Bots, Golden Tower, Death Wave, and Vault
disambiguation: This chunk is about the interaction between the Bot Cooldowns footgun, bots, sync targets, and the Vault mitigation path, not the individual mechanics. It is not a full bot upgrade guide or a medals-spending priority list.
content: Bot Cooldowns with Bots, Golden Tower, Death Wave, and Vault. The bot cooldown footgun matters because bot timings often want to sit at clean ratios relative to Golden Tower and Death Wave. Current site bot data shows Coin Bot, Amplify Bot, and Thunder Bot all move from 120-second base cooldown to a 75-second medal floor and then to 50 seconds after the full lab reduction, which is exactly why breakpoint planning matters before permanent lab levels are locked in. The source also points to a later Bot Cooldown Slider tech tree upgrade, and current vault data confirms that slider exists as a Vault node, so the mitigation path is real but late enough that the early lab mistake still qualifies as a footgun.
interaction_summary: Bot cooldown labs create permanent sync constraints against bot and Ultimate Weapon timings, while Vault later adds a Bot Cooldown Slider mitigation path.

topic: Chrono Field Range with Chrono Field, Tournaments, and Milestones
title: Chrono Field Range with Chrono Field, Tournaments, and Milestones
disambiguation: This chunk is about the interaction between the Chrono Field Range footgun, Chrono Field, tournaments, and its unlock context, not the individual mechanics. It is not a generic lab priority guide or a farming walkthrough.
content: Chrono Field Range with Chrono Field, Tournaments, and Milestones. Chrono Field Range is a contextual footgun instead of a blanket do-not-upgrade warning. The source says the extra zoom-out can lower coins per hour by pushing enemy spawns further away, but it also says the downside is usually minor compared with tournament value. Current milestone data places Chrono Field Range at Tier 7 wave 90, which fits that warning profile: by the time the lab appears, players are far enough into progression that tournament performance and specialized farm tuning both matter.
interaction_summary: Chrono Field Range can hurt some farming kill timing while still being worth maxing because its tournament value usually outweighs the coins-per-hour downside.

title: Guides Overview
disambiguation: This chunk is about the Guides mechanic itself, not its interactions. It is not about one specific build, a single stat row, or tracker-specific UI behavior.
content: Guides Overview. Guides are condensed strategy references that summarize common progression paths, farming setups, and spending priorities. They are directional rather than exhaustive, so each guide is best read as a strategic overview connected to deeper mechanic references.

title: eHP Guide Overview
disambiguation: This chunk is about the eHP Guide Overview mechanic itself, not its interactions. It is not a run log, tracker-specific UI behavior, or a generic summary outside the eHP guide.
content: eHP Guide Overview. Health builds, also called effective-health or eHP builds, prioritize health and damage reduction so the tower can survive longer waves while progression is still early. The guide is aimed mainly at the early and mid game, where health scales well through roughly Tiers 1 to 9 before later progress eventually demands a stronger damage-based transition. Because of that later ceiling, the guide treats eHP as a progression phase to outgrow rather than a forever build to max blindly. Strengths: Cheap to start. Needs no mandatory Ultimate Weapon unlock to begin. Makes early tier milestones and relic unlocks easier to reach. Weaknesses: Protector enemies are a common damage bottleneck, especially early on. The build has a lower long-term progress ceiling than late-game damage strategies. Vampire enemies can become a major source of failed runs if anti-vampire tools lag behind.

title: eHP Guide Starting Setup
disambiguation: This chunk is about the eHP Guide Starting Setup mechanic itself, not its interactions. It is not a run log, tracker-specific UI behavior, or a generic summary outside the eHP guide.
content: eHP Guide Starting Setup. Workshop: Attack should be unlocked through Rapid Fire, with Bounce Shot optional. Defense should be unlocked through Orbs, with Land Mines optional at the start. Utility should at least unlock Free Upgrades. Ultimate Weapons: No Ultimate Weapon is required to start, but Golden Tower and Black Hole are preferred economy unlocks that make the build progress faster. Cards: No card is strictly required, but the guide recommends at least 6 slots for Enemy Balance, Coins, Cash, Critical Coin, Health, and Attack Speed. Labs: No upgrade is mandatory at the start, but having all 5 labs unlocked is recommended so the build can develop properly. Bots: No bot is required, but Golden Bot, which site data labels Coin Bot, is a strong optional pickup. Modules: No module is required, but Wormhole Redirector is a major survivability boost once available.

title: eHP Guide Workshop Priorities
disambiguation: This chunk is about the eHP Guide Workshop Priorities mechanic itself, not its interactions. It is not a run log, tracker-specific UI behavior, or a generic summary outside the eHP guide.
content: eHP Guide Workshop Priorities. Workshop priority starts by maxing the shorter and cheaper upgrades, especially on the defense tab, so Free Upgrades are more likely to land on Health during a run. Once those cheap upgrades are handled, the guide shifts into direct Health and Damage spending instead of leaving both stats underfunded. A common cash-spending ratio is keeping Health and Damage close to 1:1 or 1:2 in favor of Health, because the build is meant to live longer while still clearing protectors eventually. Enemy Attack Level Skip and Enemy Health Level Skip matter later, but the guide treats them as expensive follow-up upgrades rather than opening priorities. Enemy Attack Level Skip mainly extends survivability, while Enemy Health Level Skip helps preserve protector-kill capability for longer.

title: eHP Guide Lab Priorities
disambiguation: This chunk is about the eHP Guide Lab Priorities mechanic itself, not its interactions. It is not a run log, tracker-specific UI behavior, or a generic summary outside the eHP guide.
content: eHP Guide Lab Priorities. The lab plan assumes 5 active labs and recommends unlocking all 5 if they are still missing. The early lab plan is split between raw survival, orb support, coin scaling, and long-run utility so the build can both push progression and keep farming relevant. Lab 1: Game Speed should be maxed to level 7. Lab Speed should be maxed to level 99 because the guide treats lab speedups as making the late levels worth finishing. Lab 2: Attack Speed should be maxed to level 99 because it supports knockback, damage per second, and overall survival. Lab 3: Health is recommended around level 40 to 50 so early progression improves without overcommitting to a stat that falls off later. Defense % is recommended to about level 23 because that, together with perk, card, and module support, can reach the practical 98% cap in farming. Orb Speed should be maxed to level 20 because orbs are the main killer for many eHP runs. Extra Orb Adjuster should be maxed to level 1. Extra Extra Orbs should be maxed to level 2 even though it is expensive and long term. Black Hole Damage should be maxed to level 10 so Black Hole can help clear protectors. Lab 4: Cash Bonus is recommended around level 40 to 50. Coins / Kill is recommended around level 50 to 70 depending on when Golden Tower is unlocked. Golden Tower Duration should be maxed to level 20. Golden Tower Bonus is usually worth pushing to about level 20 to 25, with duration prioritized first. Black Hole Coin Bonus should be maxed to level 20. Spotlight Coin Bonus should be maxed to level 20. Perk labs should generally be maxed, except the guide keeps Perk Wave Requirement on a 4n+1 breakpoint and treats Auto Perks as player preference. Lab 5: The fifth slot is a flex slot for unfinished priorities from Lab 3 and Lab 4. The guide also calls out Package After Boss, Crit Factor, Damage, and Damage / Meter as useful flex studies when protectors start surviving too long.

title: eHP Guide Card Priorities
disambiguation: This chunk is about the eHP Guide Card Priorities mechanic itself, not its interactions. It is not a run log, tracker-specific UI behavior, or a generic summary outside the eHP guide.
content: eHP Guide Card Priorities. Health: Directly increases survivability and is the obvious core card for the build. Extra Defense: Adds more effective health by improving damage reduction. Extra Orbs: Acts as a primary killer for most normal enemies. Attack Speed: Improves crowd control and survival the same way the lab priority does. Plasma Cannon: Cuts boss-hit requirements, with level 1 reducing bosses to 2 thorn-assisted hits and level 7 reducing that to 1. Damage: Helps clear protectors once survivability is stable enough. Berserker: Adds more damage support for protector clearing. Energy Net: The guide recommends avoiding it for eHP because trapping bosses can let other enemies hide behind them and sneak in extra hits.

title: eHP Guide Ultimate Weapon Support
disambiguation: This chunk is about the eHP Guide Ultimate Weapon Support mechanic itself, not its interactions. It is not a run log, tracker-specific UI behavior, or a generic summary outside the eHP guide.
content: eHP Guide Ultimate Weapon Support. No Ultimate Weapon is mandatory, but Spotlight and Black Hole are the first support weapons the guide recommends for standard health builds. Spotlight helps by raising damage against protectors while also adding a coin bonus. Black Hole helps because its percent-health damage can remove protectors much more efficiently once its duration and damage lab are developed. Death Wave is also called out as a very useful health-build weapon. Chrono Field is presented as a later bridge weapon when the account is already thinking about its next strategy, because Chrono Field needs heavy stones and long labs before it feels strong.

title: eHP Guide Round Triage
disambiguation: This chunk is about the eHP Guide Round Triage mechanic itself, not its interactions. It is not a run log, tracker-specific UI behavior, or a generic summary outside the eHP guide.
content: eHP Guide Round Triage. Bosses one-shot the tower: Add more health. Multiple boss hits in a row kill the run: Add more lifesteal support through Attack Speed, Damage, and Crit Factor so bosses stop chaining hits uncontested. Other enemies are killing the run: Add more crowd control, especially through Attack Speed and Orbs. Protectors are letting other enemies leak through: Add more damage so protectors stop acting as a survival wall. The run needs rebalancing after a failure: Adjust with coins and labs between runs or rebalance cash spending during the next run instead of repeating the same stat pattern blindly.

title: eHP Guide Transition Tools
disambiguation: This chunk is about the eHP Guide Transition Tools mechanic itself, not its interactions. It is not a run log, tracker-specific UI behavior, or a generic summary outside the eHP guide.
content: eHP Guide Transition Tools. Chrono Field is framed as a long-term chip-reduction pickup once the build is nearing its limit and preparing for a later strategy change. Garlic Thorns is called out as an important anti-vampire tool because vampires are a frequent cause of health-build deaths. Orb Boss Hit levels 1 to 3 can combine with level 6 Plasma Cannon so thorn-assisted boss kills drop to a single hit, but the guide treats that research as mostly a transition tool for later damage builds rather than a core eHP priority.

title: Gems Guide Overview
disambiguation: This chunk is about the Gems Guide Overview mechanic itself, not its interactions. It is not a generic gem-spending summary outside the gems guide, a live inventory state, or a shop calculator output.
content: Gems Guide Overview. Gems are acquired slowly enough that inefficient spending decisions can delay account progress for a long time. The guide therefore sequences gem spending around permanent bottlenecks first, then around the minimum card and module shell needed to keep runs productive. Relevant site data matches that framing because Gems are shared across Lab Slots, cards, Card Slots, Module Acquisition, and Lab Rushing rather than belonging to one isolated upgrade path.

title: Gems Guide Lab Slots
disambiguation: This chunk is about the Gems Guide Lab Slots mechanic itself, not its interactions. It is not a generic gem-spending summary outside the gems guide, a live inventory state, or a shop calculator output.
content: Gems Guide Lab Slots. Labs are treated as the main early bottleneck, so the guide pushes Lab slot 2 first, then returns to Lab slot 3, Lab slot 4, and Lab slot 5 as soon as the basic card shell for each stage is in place. Site data puts Lab slot costs at 100, 400, 1400, and 3000 Gems for slots 2 through 5, with 4900 total Gems needed to reach all five lab slots. Because Lab Slots permanently increase parallel research capacity, the guide treats finishing all five slots as the baseline long-term gem goal before any heavy card or rush spending.

topic: Gems Guide Early Cards and Slots
title: Gems Guide Early Cards and Slots
disambiguation: This chunk is about the Gems Guide Early Cards and Slots mechanic itself, not its interactions. It is not a generic gem-spending summary outside the gems guide, a live inventory state, or a shop calculator output.
content: Gems Guide Early Cards and Slots. After Lab slot 2: Unlock Attack Speed, Enemy Balance, and Coins. Buy enough Card Slots to equip those three cards together instead of leaving one of them unused. After Lab slot 3: Add Health and Cash to the early shell. Buy enough Card Slots to run the five-card setup at the same time. After Lab slot 4: Unlock two of Critical Coin, Wave Skip, and Extra Orb. Buy two more Card Slots so those additions can actually be equipped when they become relevant.
mechanics: Gems Guide Early Cards and Slots

title: Gems Guide First Epic Modules
disambiguation: This chunk is about the Gems Guide First Epic Modules mechanic itself, not its interactions. It is not a generic gem-spending summary outside the gems guide, a live inventory state, or a shop calculator output.
content: Gems Guide First Epic Modules. After Lab slot 5, the guide recommends getting one Epic module of each type before chasing particular uniques. Site data says Module Acquisition unlocks at Tier 2 Wave 90, gives 10 module tickets on unlock, and costs 20 Gems for a single draw or 200 Gems for a ten-pull, so this first module sweep is framed as controlled setup rather than endless gambling. The guide explicitly warns that many unique effects are not fully usable for newer accounts. Havoc Bringer depends on Rend Armor being unlocked, and many Core module effects do not matter until the matching Ultimate Weapon exists. That is why the goal of the first Epic floor is mainly higher base stats and better Sub-Module Effects access through rerolls, not perfect unique-module targeting.

title: Gems Guide Ongoing Spending Loop
disambiguation: This chunk is about the Gems Guide Ongoing Spending Loop mechanic itself, not its interactions. It is not a generic gem-spending summary outside the gems guide, a live inventory state, or a shop calculator output.
content: Gems Guide Ongoing Spending Loop. Once the first Epic floor exists, gems shift mostly toward cards while still reserving a steady amount for modules. The guide treats cards such as Plasma Cannon and Wave Accelerator as high-value hits, but it rejects hard-targeting one card before asking whether another Card Slot would help the current build more immediately. The decision rule is simple: if an already-owned card would help a lot when equipped now, buy a Card Slot; if not, keep buying and upgrading cards until another slot would create real value. Modules stay in the loop through a weekly spending cap such as 200 or 400 Gems depending on play volume, because module growth is too strong to ignore while finishing the card collection. Site data makes the tradeoff visible because Card Slot Costs rise from 50 Gems at slot 2 to 10000 Gems at slot 22, with 58400 total Gems needed to reach 22 purchased slots.

title: Gems Guide Lab Rushing
disambiguation: This chunk is about the Gems Guide Lab Rushing mechanic itself, not its interactions. It is not a generic gem-spending summary outside the gems guide, a live inventory state, or a shop calculator output.
content: Gems Guide Lab Rushing. Key labs can be rushed as needed once the account already has the slot foundation, especially Lab Speed, Attack Speed, and Chrono Field Duration when that option exists. Chrono Field Duration is not an early default because Chrono Field labs do not unlock until Tier 7 Wave 90. The guide still treats modules as often more important than lab rushing for Gems because module power and lab-boost support can outpace marginal rush value. For other labs, the guide recommends saving and rushing only when the timer is very long, with 14 or more days given as the threshold for whole-lab rushes. Site data supports that rule because Lab Rushing only skips the full remaining timer, becomes more Gem-efficient on longer researches, and improves further when labs are gold boxed.

title: Medals Guide Overview
disambiguation: This chunk is about the Medals Guide Overview mechanic itself, not its interactions. It is not a generic medal-spending summary outside the medals guide, a current-event inventory readout, or a weekly reward table.
content: Medals Guide Overview. Medals are treated as a slower, scarcer event currency than the options they compete with, so bad spends can block more important permanent gains for multiple events.
