title: Milestones Overview
disambiguation: This chunk is about the Milestones mechanic itself, not its interactions. It is not about unrelated tracker state, individual lab formulas, or non-milestone reward systems.
content: Milestones Overview. Milestones span Tier 1 through Tier 21 with a separate standard and premium reward track at each wave threshold. Standard track milestone rewards carry most permanent system unlocks, while premium track milestones lean harder into extra resources, cosmetics, and end-of-tier relic payouts. Tier progression unlocks the next tier at wave 100 through Tier 14, then shifts to wave 300 from Tier 15 onward. Milestone totals are tracked separately per tier and per track, so standard rewards and premium rewards should not be merged into one unlock list. Core system unlocks on the standard track include Labs (T1 W30), Tournaments (T1 W60), Events (T1 W70), Modules (T2 W90), Unlock Perks (T2 W150), Guilds (T3 W10), Workshop Respec (T4 W30), Ban Perks (T5 W40), Extra Orb Adjuster (T6 W50), Wall Health (T8 W10), Workshop Enhancement (T12 W60), Shatter Shards (T16 W40), Card Mastery Unlock (T16 W100), Assist Module (T19 W40), Group 4 BC Labs (T21 W100).

title: Milestone Standard Track
disambiguation: This chunk is about the Milestone Standard Track mechanic itself, not its interactions. It is not about unrelated tracker state, individual lab formulas, or non-milestone reward systems.
content: Milestone Standard Track. The standard milestone track is the main progression path for permanent feature unlocks, tier advancement, and many system-level power spikes. Early standard-track unlocks include Labs at T1 W30, Tournaments at T1 W60, Events at T1 W70, Max Interest at T1 W80, Lab Speed at T1 W150, More Round Stats at T1 W250, Card Presets at T1 W400, Buy Multiplier at T2 W20, Range at T2 W30, Workshop Attack Discount at T2 W40, Workshop Defense Discount at T2 W50, Workshop Utility Discount at T2 W60. Later standard-track unlocks continue with Wall Invincibility at T12 W10, Workshop Enhancement at T12 W60, Max Rend Armor Multi at T13 W10, Ranged Enemy Range Lab at T13 W80, BH Disable Ranged at T14 W20, Wall Fortification at T14 W40, Card: UW Crit at T14 W50, Recharge Barrage at T14 W60.

title: Milestone Premium Track
disambiguation: This chunk is about the Milestone Premium Track mechanic itself, not its interactions. It is not about unrelated tracker state, individual lab formulas, or non-milestone reward systems.
content: Milestone Premium Track. The premium milestone track stays separate from the standard unlock path and mainly adds extra resource payouts, cosmetics, and end-of-tier relic-style rewards. At the top end, Tier 21 premium alone totals 8T Coins, 2,330 Gems, and 740 Stones. Premium cosmetic rewards include Donut Skin (T2), Butterfly Skin (T5), Mush-mush Skin (T8), Cat Skin (T11), Panda Skin (T14), Dragon Skin (T17), Cyber Skin (T20).

title: Milestone Tier Progression
disambiguation: This chunk is about the Milestone Tier Progression mechanic itself, not its interactions. It is not about unrelated tracker state, individual lab formulas, or non-milestone reward systems.
content: Milestone Tier Progression. Milestone tier progression determines when the next tier becomes playable, so it controls when the account can start accessing that next tier's unlock table. Early tier progression follows Tier 2 at T1 W100, Tier 3 at T2 W100, Tier 4 at T3 W100, Tier 5 at T4 W100, Tier 6 at T5 W100, Tier 7 at T6 W100, Tier 8 at T7 W100, Tier 9 at T8 W100, Tier 10 at T9 W100, Tier 11 at T10 W100, Tier 12 at T11 W100, Tier 13 at T12 W100, Tier 14 at T13 W100, Tier 15 at T14 W100. Late tier progression shifts to wave 300 and follows Tier 16 at T15 W300, Tier 17 at T16 W300, Tier 18 at T17 W300, Tier 19 at T18 W300, Tier 20 at T19 W300, Tier 21 at T20 W300.

title: Milestone Tier Totals
disambiguation: This chunk is about the Milestone Tier Totals mechanic itself, not its interactions. It is not about unrelated tracker state, individual lab formulas, or non-milestone reward systems.
content: Milestone Tier Totals. Tier 1 totals: Standard gives 1,660 Coins, 235 Gems, and 5 Stones, while Premium gives 141,450 Coins, 360 Gems, and 35 Stones. Tier 10 totals: Standard gives 20m Coins, 535 Gems, and 60 Stones, while Premium gives 105m Coins, 920 Gems, and 170 Stones. Tier 16 totals: Standard gives 30b Coins, 750 Gems, and 225 Stones, while Premium gives 180b Coins, 1,260 Gems, and 440 Stones. Tier 21 totals: Standard gives 1T Coins, 1,750 Gems, and 385 Stones, while Premium gives 8T Coins, 2,330 Gems, and 740 Stones.

topic: Milestone Standard Track with Milestone Premium Track
title: Milestone Standard Track with Milestone Premium Track
disambiguation: This chunk is about the interaction between the Standard and Premium milestone tracks, not the individual mechanics. It is not about unrelated event boosters, lab costs, or tracker UI features.
content: Milestone Standard Track with Milestone Premium Track. Every milestone tier has both a Standard track and a Premium track at the same wave breakpoints. The Standard track is where most permanent gameplay unlocks live, including tier advancement and major system unlocks. The Premium track does not replace those unlocks. It adds extra coins, gems, stones, cosmetics, and high-tier relic-style rewards on top of the Standard ladder.
interaction_summary: Each milestone tier has separate Standard and Premium tracks, with Standard carrying most unlocks and Premium adding extra resources and cosmetics.

topic: Milestone Tier Progression with Milestone Tier Totals
title: Milestone Tier Progression with Milestone Tier Totals
disambiguation: This chunk is about the interaction between Milestone Tier Progression and Milestone Tier Totals, not the individual mechanics. It is not about event medals, guild tokens, or unrelated unlock trees.
content: Milestone Tier Progression with Milestone Tier Totals. Milestone Tier Progression controls when the next tier opens, while Milestone Tier Totals describe how much resource value each tier pays out on Standard and Premium. Early progression uses wave 100 tier unlocks, but late progression moves to wave 300 before the next tier opens. As tiers rise, total coins, gems, and stones per track also rise, which is why late milestone tiers matter for both account progression and long-run resource income.
interaction_summary: Higher milestone tiers both unlock later progression and increase the total resource payouts available on each track.

title: Modules Overview
disambiguation: This chunk is about the Modules mechanic itself, not its interactions. It is not about unrelated tracker state, implementation details, or other game systems.
content: Modules Overview. This file reorganizes module knowledge into the same keyed mechanic format used by other deterministic knowledge sources. The original raw source remains preserved in public/knowledge/modules for side-by-side comparison. Definition: Modules are equipable gear items that provide main effects, sub-module effects, and sometimes unique effects. Type: System. Domain: Progression. Section: Modules. Category: Gear. Behavior: Modules come in four types: Cannon, Armor, Generator, and Core. Modules are unlocked at Tier 2 Wave 90. Modules can be acquired through module tickets or Gems.

title: Module Types
disambiguation: This chunk is about the Module Types mechanic itself, not its interactions. It is not about unrelated tracker state, implementation details, or other game systems.
content: Module Types. Definition: Module Types split modules into Cannon, Armor, Generator, and Core families. Type: Classification. Domain: Modules. Section: Modules. Category: Families. Aliases: module families. Behavior: Cannon modules focus on Attack. Armor modules focus on Defense. Generator modules focus on Utility. Core modules focus on Ultimate Weapons.

title: Module Acquisition
disambiguation: This chunk is about the Module Acquisition mechanic itself, not its interactions. It is not about unrelated tracker state, implementation details, or other game systems.
content: Module Acquisition. Definition: Module Acquisition is the process of unlocking and drawing modules with tickets or Gems. Type: Acquisition System. Domain: Modules. Section: Modules. Category: Pulls. Aliases: acquiring modules. Behavior: Modules unlock at Tier 2 Wave 90. Players receive 10 module tickets when modules first unlock. Modules can be bought for 20 Gems as a single draw or 200 Gems as a ten-pull.

title: Module Pull Rates
disambiguation: This chunk is about the Module Pull Rates mechanic itself, not its interactions. It is not about unrelated tracker state, implementation details, or other game systems.
content: Module Pull Rates. Definition: Module Pull Rates determine the rarity distribution for purchased module draws. Type: Draw Rates. Domain: Modules. Section: Modules. Category: Pulls. Aliases: module rates. Behavior: Common module rate is 68.5%. Rare module rate is 29%. Epic module rate is 2.5%. Bad luck protection guarantees an Epic module if 150 purchases pass without one. Every ten-pull guarantees at least one Rare module.

title: Module Banners
disambiguation: This chunk is about the Module Banners mechanic itself, not its interactions. It is not about unrelated tracker state, implementation details, or other game systems.
content: Module Banners. Definition: Module Banners control which module pools and rate modifiers are active for module pulls. Type: Banner System. Domain: Modules. Section: Modules. Category: Pulls. Aliases: featured banner; standard banner. Behavior: The standard banner uses normal Epic pull distributions. Modules already owned at Ancestral 5 stars are less likely to be pulled on the standard banner. The featured banner gives 50% of Epic pulls to the featured module. Featured banners last two weeks and are followed by a one-week break.

title: Module Upgrading
disambiguation: This chunk is about the Module Upgrading mechanic itself, not its interactions. It is not about unrelated tracker state, implementation details, or other game systems.
content: Module Upgrading. Definition: Module Upgrading uses shards and coins to raise a module's level and improve its main stat. Type: Upgrade System. Domain: Modules. Section: Modules. Category: Progression. Aliases: leveling modules. Behavior: Module leveling increases the main stat only. The maximum level depends on the module's current rarity. Merging to a higher rarity raises the level cap without resetting the current level.

title: Module Level Caps
disambiguation: This chunk is about the Module Level Caps mechanic itself, not its interactions. It is not about unrelated tracker state, implementation details, or other game systems.
content: Module Level Caps. Definition: Module Level Caps define the highest module level available at each rarity tier. Type: Level Cap Table. Domain: Modules. Section: Modules. Category: Progression. Aliases: max module level. Behavior: Rare caps at level 30. Rare+ caps at level 40. Epic caps at level 60. Epic+ caps at level 80. Legendary caps at level 100. Legendary+ caps at level 120. Mythic caps at level 140. Mythic+ caps at level 160. Ancestral caps at level 200. Ancestral star tiers continue to 300 at Ancestral 5.

title: Module Restore
disambiguation: This chunk is about the Module Restore mechanic itself, not its interactions. It is not about unrelated tracker state, implementation details, or other game systems.
content: Module Restore. Definition: Module Restore resets level investment and returns shard and coin spending. Type: Reset Rule. Domain: Modules. Section: Modules. Category: Progression. Aliases: restore button; reset modules. Behavior: Module Restore costs no resources. Module Restore returns all spent shards and coins. Reroll shards and Gems are not returned. Sub-module effects are retained until the module is leveled again, even if those effects normally require higher levels.

title: Module Boss Drops
disambiguation: This chunk is about the Module Boss Drops mechanic itself, not its interactions. It is not about unrelated tracker state, implementation details, or other game systems.
content: Module Boss Drops. Definition: Module Boss Drops determine boss rewards for reroll shards and module drops. Type: Drop System. Domain: Bosses. Section: Modules. Category: Drops. Aliases: boss module drops. Behavior: Bosses can drop reroll shards as well as Common and Rare modules. Reroll shards have a 15% drop chance. Common modules start at a 2% drop chance. Rare modules start at a 0.5% drop chance. Boss reroll shard quantity increases by tier. Module drop rates can be increased by labs.

title: Module Merging
disambiguation: This chunk is about the Module Merging mechanic itself, not its interactions. It is not about unrelated tracker state, implementation details, or other game systems.
content: Module Merging. Definition: Module Merging raises a module's rarity, main stat value, scaling, and level cap. Type: Merge System. Domain: Modules. Section: Modules. Category: Progression. Aliases: merging modules. Behavior: Common modules cannot be merged. Rare modules can merge up to Legendary+. Epic modules can merge up to Ancestral 5 stars. Merging does not reset the current module level. Rare modules never gain unique effects through merging. Rare modules keep their original name and do not become matching Epic uniques.

title: Module Merge Materials
disambiguation: This chunk is about the Module Merge Materials mechanic itself, not its interactions. It is not about unrelated tracker state, implementation details, or other game systems.
content: Module Merge Materials. Definition: Module Merge Materials specify the exact same-module and wildcard requirements for each merge step. Type: Merge Materials. Domain: Modules. Section: Modules. Category: Progression. Aliases: merge materials; wildcard modules. Behavior: The primary module is always the first module selected for merging. A module icon requirement means the material must be that same named module at the shown rarity. A wildcard requirement can be any module of the same type and shown rarity. Ancestral star upgrades require a natural Epic+ copy of the same module and each star increases the main effect.

title: Module Stats
disambiguation: This chunk is about the Module Stats mechanic itself, not its interactions. It is not about unrelated tracker state, implementation details, or other game systems.
content: Module Stats. Definition: Module Stats are split into Main Effect, Sub-Module Effects, and Unique Effects. Type: Stat Structure. Domain: Modules. Section: Modules. Category: Effects. Aliases: module stat types. Behavior: Every module has a Main Effect. Modules can unlock Sub-Module Effect slots as they level. Unique Effects only exist on naturally drawn Epic modules.

title: Module Main Effect
disambiguation: This chunk is about the Module Main Effect mechanic itself, not its interactions. It is not about unrelated tracker state, implementation details, or other game systems.
content: Module Main Effect. Definition: Module Main Effect is the primary stat bonus granted by a module and the only effect increased by module level. Type: Main Stat. Domain: Modules. Section: Modules. Category: Effects. Aliases: main effect. Behavior: Main Effect maps to tower damage for Cannon, health for Armor, coin bonus for Generator, and Ultimate Weapon damage for Core. Only module level upgrades change the Main Effect. Module levels 41, 101, 141, 161, 201, and 241 unlock additional Sub-Module Effect slots.

title: Module Sub-Module Effects
disambiguation: This chunk is about the Module Sub-Module Effects mechanic itself, not its interactions. It is not about unrelated tracker state, implementation details, or other game systems.
content: Module Sub-Module Effects. Definition: Module Sub-Module Effects are rerollable secondary stats chosen from a family-specific pool. Type: Substats. Domain: Modules. Section: Modules. Category: Effects. Aliases: substats; sub-module effects. Behavior: Sub-Module Effect pools depend on the module family. The maximum rarity of a substat matches the module's current rarity, but the current rolled substat can be below that ceiling. Substat rarity chances are Common 46.2%, Rare 40%, Epic 10%, Legendary 2.5%, Mythic 1.0%, and Ancestral 0.3%.

title: Module Reroll Locks
disambiguation: This chunk is about the Module Reroll Locks mechanic itself, not its interactions. It is not about unrelated tracker state, implementation details, or other game systems.
content: Module Reroll Locks. Definition: Module Reroll Locks protect chosen substats from rerolling at the cost of higher reroll-shard prices. Type: Reroll Cost Rule. Domain: Modules. Section: Modules. Category: Effects. Aliases: lock costs; locked substats. Behavior: Zero locks costs 10 reroll shards. One lock costs 40 reroll shards. Two locks costs 160 reroll shards. Three locks costs 500 reroll shards. Four locks costs 1000 reroll shards. Five locks costs 1600 reroll shards. Six locks costs 2250 reroll shards. Seven locks costs 3000 reroll shards. Auto Roll can reroll rapidly until acceptable effects and rarities are found. Effect bans remove banned effects from the reroll pool when researched.

title: Module Unique Effects
disambiguation: This chunk is about the Unique Effects mechanic itself, not its interactions. It is not about unrelated tracker state, implementation details, or other game systems.
content: Module Unique Effects. Definition: Unique Effects are special module abilities present only on modules that were naturally drawn as Epics. Type: Unique Effect Rule. Domain: Modules. Section: Modules. Category: Effects. Aliases: unique module effects. Behavior: Epic modules drawn from pulls have Unique Effects. Rare modules merged to Epic or higher never gain Unique Effects. Natural Epic modules retain their Unique Effects through higher rarities.

title: Assist Modules
disambiguation: This chunk is about the Assist Modules mechanic itself, not its interactions. It is not about unrelated tracker state, implementation details, or other game systems.
content: Assist Modules. Definition: Assist Modules let a second module be equipped in the same slot for weaker versions of its effects. Type: Assist System. Domain: Modules. Section: Modules. Category: Assist Modules. Aliases: assist module; assist slot. Behavior: Assist Modules unlock at Tier 19 Wave 40. Assist slots cost 1000 stones each to unlock. An assist module cannot share the same name as the main module in that slot. Assist module level is separate from the main module level. Assist efficiency can be improved with stones and with assist-module labs unlocked at Tier 19 Wave 50. Assist modules do not bypass hard caps such as defense, Chrono Field slow, Wall rebuild, Shockwave Frequency, Death Defy, or Inner Land Mine cooldown caps. As of v27.1, all assist-module multiplier stats are multiplicative. Quantity assist substats use FLOOR, not ROUND, so values only add quantity once the floored threshold is reached.

title: Assist Module Unique Rarity Costs
disambiguation: This chunk is about the Assist Module Unique Rarity Costs mechanic itself, not its interactions. It is not about unrelated tracker state, implementation details, or other game systems.
content: Assist Module Unique Rarity Costs. Definition: Assist Module Unique Rarity Costs define the stone spending required to raise assist unique-effect quality. Type: Stone Cost Ladder. Domain: Stones. Section: Modules. Category: Assist Modules. Aliases: assist rarity cost. Behavior: Unlocking assist unique effect quality at Epic costs 1000 stones. Raising it to Legendary costs 1000 stones. Raising it to Mythic costs 1200 stones. Raising it to Ancestral costs 1400 stones. The listed total is 4600 stones.

topic: Module Acquisition with Gems, Module Tickets, and Module Banners
title: Module Acquisition with Gems, Module Tickets, and Module Banners
disambiguation: This chunk is about the interaction between Module Acquisition, Gems, Module Tickets, and Module Banners, not the individual mechanics. It is not about substats, merge materials, or unrelated currencies.
content: Module Acquisition with Gems, Module Tickets, and Module Banners. Module Acquisition begins once Modules unlock, and it can spend Gems or Module Tickets to create pulls. Module Banners determine how those Gems or Module Tickets translate into actual Epic distributions, including featured-module weighting. This means the value of Module Acquisition depends both on the resource spent and on which Module Banners are currently active.
interaction_summary: Module Acquisition consumes Gems or Module Tickets, and Module Banners decide which Epic distributions apply to those purchases.

topic: Module Pull Rates with Bad Luck Protection and Ten Pulls
title: Module Pull Rates with Bad Luck Protection and Ten Pulls
disambiguation: This chunk is about the interaction between Module Pull Rates, Bad Luck Protection, and Ten Pulls, not the individual mechanics. It is not about merge rules, substats, or unrelated drop systems.
content: Module Pull Rates with Bad Luck Protection and Ten Pulls. Module Pull Rates provide the base Common, Rare, and Epic odds. Bad Luck Protection overrides those odds only after 150 purchases pass without an Epic module. Ten Pulls add a separate guarantee for at least one Rare module, so the live outcome is a combination of base Module Pull Rates and guarantee rules.
interaction_summary: Module Pull Rates define the base draw odds, while Bad Luck Protection and Ten Pulls add guarantee rules on top of those odds.

topic: Module Upgrading with Module Level Caps and Module Merging
title: Module Upgrading with Module Level Caps and Module Merging
disambiguation: This chunk is about the interaction between Module Upgrading, Module Level Caps, and Module Merging, not the individual mechanics. It is not about banner odds, boss drops, or unrelated currencies.
content: Module Upgrading with Module Level Caps and Module Merging. Module Upgrading spends shards and coins to increase level, but it can only move until the active Module Level Caps for the current rarity. Module Level Caps in site data are: Common 20, Rare 30, Rare + 40, Epic 60, Epic + 80, Legendary 100, Legendary + 120, Mythic 140, Mythic + 160, Ancestral 200, Ancestral 1 220, Ancestral 2 240, Ancestral 3 260, Ancestral 4 280, Ancestral 5 300. Module Merging changes the rarity state, which in turn raises the Module Level Caps while preserving the already-earned module level.
interaction_summary: Module Upgrading spends shards and coins up to the current Module Level Caps, and Module Merging raises those caps without wiping current levels.

topic: Module Boss Drops with Lab Research
title: Module Boss Drops with Lab Research
disambiguation: This chunk is about the interaction between Module Boss Drops and Lab Research, not the individual mechanics. It is not about module banners, merge paths, or unrelated lab families.
content: Module Boss Drops with Lab Research. Module Boss Drops provide the baseline reroll-shard, Common-module, and Rare-module boss rewards. The wiki extraction explicitly notes that the module drop rates from Module Boss Drops can be improved by Lab Research. This makes Lab Research a scaling layer on top of the base Module Boss Drops table rather than a separate drop system.
interaction_summary: Module Boss Drops start from base reroll-shard and module rates, and Lab Research can increase the module-drop side of those boss rewards.

topic: Module Sub-Module Effects with Module Reroll Locks, Auto Roll, and Effect Bans
title: Module Sub-Module Effects with Module Reroll Locks, Auto Roll, and Effect Bans
disambiguation: This chunk is about the interaction between Module Sub-Module Effects, Module Reroll Locks, Auto Roll, and Effect Bans, not the individual mechanics. It is not about main stat leveling, banner odds, or unrelated merge systems.
content: Module Sub-Module Effects with Module Reroll Locks, Auto Roll, and Effect Bans. Module Sub-Module Effects are the pool being rerolled when players chase better secondary stats. Module Reroll Locks increase reroll cost to preserve chosen substats, while Auto Roll automates repeated rerolls until acceptable effects or rarities appear. If Effect Bans are researched, Effect Bans further narrow the Module Sub-Module Effects pool by excluding banned results from rerolls.
interaction_summary: Module Sub-Module Effects are rerolled through Auto Roll or manual rerolls, while Module Reroll Locks protect chosen effects and Effect Bans remove forbidden effects from the reroll pool.

topic: Assist Modules with Stones, Assist Module Labs, and Hard Caps
title: Assist Modules with Stones, Assist Module Labs, and Hard Caps
disambiguation: This chunk is about the interaction between Assist Modules, Stones, Assist Module Labs, and Hard Caps, not the individual mechanics. It is not about banner odds, normal merge paths, or unrelated tracker pages.
content: Assist Modules with Stones, Assist Module Labs, and Hard Caps. Assist Modules require Stones both to unlock assist slots and to improve assist-side quality or efficiency. Assist Module Labs add extra scaling to assist bonuses and assist substats after those labs unlock. Even with Stones investment and Assist Module Labs, Assist Modules still obey Hard Caps such as defense, Chrono Field slow, Wall rebuild, Shockwave Frequency, Death Defy, and Inner Land Mine cooldown caps.
interaction_summary: Assist Modules spend Stones for unlock and quality, use Assist Module Labs for efficiency scaling, and still remain bounded by the game's Hard Caps.

topic: Cannon Module Substats with Assist Module Labs
title: Cannon Module Substats with Assist Module Labs
disambiguation: This chunk is about the interaction between Cannon Module Substats, Assist Module Substats - Cannon, and Assist Module Bonus - Cannon, not the individual mechanics. It is not about unrelated module banners, merge materials, or other module families.
content: Cannon Module Substats with Assist Module Labs. Cannon Module Substats defines the rerollable secondary stat pool for Cannon modules. Assist Module Substats - Cannon increases the assist-side substats for Cannon modules, while Assist Module Bonus - Cannon improves the assist-side bonus values. These labs matter only for Assist Modules and do not replace the normal Cannon Module Substats pool on the primary module itself.
interaction_summary: Assist Module Substats - Cannon and Assist Module Bonus - Cannon increase the weaker assist-side version of Cannon Module Substats.

title: Perks Overview
disambiguation: This chunk is about the Perks mechanic itself, not its interactions. It is not a perk pick recommendation or unrelated tool guidance.
content: Perks Overview. Perks are run-based advantages earned during a round. Perks are unlocked through labs after the Unlock Perks milestone unlock at Tier 2 Wave 150. Perks start appearing at wave 200 once the unlock path is complete. Perk pools are split into standard 65%, ultimate weapon 20%, trade off 15%.

title: Perk Wave Requirement
disambiguation: This chunk is about the Perk Wave Requirement mechanic itself, not its interactions. It is not a perk pick recommendation or unrelated tool guidance.
content: Perk Wave Requirement. Base wave brackets are 200 waves from 0 perks selected, 250 waves from 20 perks selected, 300 waves from 30 perks selected, 350 waves from 40 perks selected. Formula: Waves Required = (Base Waves Required - Waves Required Lab) × (1 - (Perk Wave Requirement Perk × (1 + Standard Perk Bonus / 100))). Use the formula to find the first perk timing for each base-wave bracket. If the result includes a decimal, round it down before multiplying by perk count. Example: SPB 8% and 3 Perk Wave Requirement perks gives 64.8%, so (200 - 3) × (1 - 0.648) = 69.344, which floors to 69 waves.

title: Perk Choice
disambiguation: This chunk is about the Perk Choice mechanic itself, not its interactions. It is not a perk pick recommendation or unrelated tool guidance.
content: Perk Choice. Base perk choice count is 2 and can be increased to a maximum of 4 through Perk Option Quantity. First Perk Choice guarantees the selected first perk as the top option on the first offering. Auto Pick Perks always chooses the top choice shown in the list. Auto Pick Ranking overrides First Perk Choice if a higher-ranked perk is available in that first offering. It is possible for all available choices to be trade-off perks even when other perk types remain in the pool.

title: Standard Perk Math
disambiguation: This chunk is about the Standard Perk Math mechanic itself, not its interactions. It is not a perk pick recommendation or unrelated tool guidance.
content: Standard Perk Math. Additive perks such as Defense Percent and Perk Wave Requirement use Base Value × Quantity × (1 + Standard Perk Bonus). Multiplicative perks such as Coin Bonus, Health, and Damage use (1 + Base Value × Quantity) × (1 + Standard Perk Bonus).

title: Standard Perks
disambiguation: This chunk is about the Standard Perks mechanic itself, not its interactions. It is not a perk pick recommendation or unrelated tool guidance.
content: Standard Perks. x1.20 Max Health (qty 5), x1.15 Damage (qty 5), x1.15 All Coin Bonuses (qty 5), x1.15 Defense Absolute (qty 5), x1.15 Cash Bonus (qty 5), x1.75 Health Regen (qty 5), Interest x1.50 (qty 5), Land Mine Damage x3.50 (qty 5), Free Upgrade Chance for All +5.0% (qty 5), Defense Percent +4.00 (qty 5), Bounce Shot +2 (qty 3), Perk Wave Requirement -20.00% (qty 3), Orbs +1 (qty 2), Unlock a Random Ultimate Weapon (qty 1), Increase Max Game Speed by +1.00 (qty 1) Bounce Shot +2 is unavailable if Bounce Shot has not been unlocked. Standard perk bonus is increased by the Standard Perk Bonus lab. When Standard Perk Bonus is maxed, Increase Max Game Speed by +1.00 becomes +1.25, making the displayed cap 6.3 while the actual cap is 6.25.

title: Ultimate Weapon Perks
disambiguation: This chunk is about the Ultimate Weapon Perks mechanic itself, not its interactions. It is not a perk pick recommendation or unrelated tool guidance.
content: Ultimate Weapon Perks. 4 More Smart Missiles (qty 1), Swamp Radius x1.5 (qty 1), +1 Wave on Death Wave (qty 1), Extra Set of Inner Mines (qty 1), Golden Tower Bonus x1.5 (qty 1), Chain Lightning Damage x2 (qty 1), Chrono Field Duration +5s (qty 1), Black Hole Duration +12.0s (qty 1), Spotlight Damage Bonus x1.5 (qty 1) Ultimate Weapon perks only appear when the affected weapon is unlocked. If the player unlocks a weapon through the random ultimate weapon perk, that weapon-specific perk can then appear during the same run. Golden Tower Bonus x1.5 does not apply to the Golden Tower bonus submodule effect.

title: Random Ultimate Weapon Perk
disambiguation: This chunk is about the Random Ultimate Weapon Perk mechanic itself, not its interactions. It is not a perk pick recommendation or unrelated tool guidance.
content: Random Ultimate Weapon Perk. The random ultimate weapon perk picks a weapon the player does not already own and grants a semi-upgraded version for that run. Unlocking a weapon this way does not unlock the related labs for that run. Relevant module substats still affect the granted weapon during the run. When all ultimate weapons are already owned, the random ultimate weapon perk is removed from the pool. Random UW stat packages: Chain Lightning = stone value 700, Damage x46, Quantity 3, Chance 15.5%; Smart Missiles = stone value 741, Damage x42, Quantity 11, Cooldown 130s; Death Wave = stone value 1009, Damage x46, Quantity 2, Cooldown 210s; Chrono Field = stone value 1824, Duration 22s, Speed Reduction 40%, Cooldown 120s; Inner Land Mines = stone value 600, Damage x16, Quantity 5, Cooldown 130s; Golden Tower = stone value 1639, Bonus x9.0, Duration 30s, Cooldown 230s; Poison Swamp = stone value 715, Damage x43, Duration 50s, Cooldown 90s; Black Hole = stone value 984, Size 50m, Duration 20s, Cooldown 130s; Spotlight = stone value 2426, Bonus x27.6, Angle 45, Quantity 1.

content: Trade-off Perks. x1.50 Tower Damage, but Bosses Have 8x Health (qty 1), x1.80 Coins, but Tower Max Health -70% (qty 1), Enemies Have -50% Health, but Tower Health Regen and Lifesteal -90% (qty 1), Enemies Damage -50%, but Tower Damage -50% (qty 1), Ranged Enemies Attack Distance Reduced, but Tower Ranged Enemies Damage x3 (qty 1), Enemies Speed -40%, but Enemies Damage x2.5 (qty 1), x12.00 Cash Per Wave, but Enemy Kills Don't Give Cash (qty 1), Tower Health Regen x8.00, but Tower Max Health -60% (qty 1), Boss Health -70%, but Boss Speed +50% (qty 1), Lifesteal x2.50, but Knockback Force -70% (qty 1) Improve Trade-Off Perks increases the benefit side of trade-off perks. title: Perk Labs
disambiguation: This chunk is about the Perk Labs mechanic itself, not its interactions. It is not a perk pick recommendation or unrelated tool guidance.
content: Perk Labs. Unlock Perks: Unlocks perk access and enables the other perk labs after completion. Unlock: Milestones Tier 2 Wave 150. Levels: 1. Waves Required: Reduces the base waves required between perk offers. Unlock: After Unlock Perks is completed. Levels: 100. Standard Perk Bonus: Scales standard perks using separate additive and multiplicative formulas. Unlock: After Unlock Perks is completed. Levels: 1. First Perk Choice: Guarantees the selected first perk as the top option on the first offering of the run. Unlock: Milestones Tier 2 Wave 250 and Unlock Perks completed. Levels: 1. Improve Trade-Off Perks: Improves the benefit side of trade-off perks except the ranged-enemy-distance trade-off. Unlock: Milestones Tier 2 Wave 400 and Unlock Perks completed. Levels: 10. Auto Pick Perks: Automatically picks the first perk listed when a perk offer appears. Unlock: Milestones Tier 4 Wave 50 and Unlock Perks completed. Levels: 1. Perk Option Quantity: Raises the number of perk choices from 2 up to 4. Unlock: Milestones Tier 4 Wave 80 and Unlock Perks completed. Levels: 2. Ban Perks: Allows perks to be banned from appearing during a run. Unlock: Milestones Tier 5 Wave 40 and Unlock Perks completed. Levels: 8. Auto Pick Ranking: Lets players rank which perks auto-pick should prioritize, and it overrides First Perk Choice when both are present. Unlock: Milestones Tier 6 Wave 10 and Auto Pick Perks completed. Levels: 32.

title: Perks with Milestones
disambiguation: This chunk is about the interaction between Perks and Milestones, not the individual mechanics. It is not about event timing, workshop values, or unrelated round systems.
content: Perks with Milestones. Perks are not available from the start of account progression. Milestones unlock the Unlock Perks lab at Tier 2 Wave 150, and that lab must then be completed before perks can appear in runs. Once that unlock chain is finished, perk offers begin at wave 200 and the rest of the perk-lab tree becomes available.
interaction_summary: Perks only come online after Milestones unlock the perk system path at Tier 2 Wave 150.

title: Perk Choice with Perk Labs
disambiguation: This chunk is about the interaction between Perk Choice and Perk Labs, not the individual mechanics. It is not about perk probability weights, event shops, or unrelated automation systems.
content: Perk Choice with Perk Labs. Perk Choice starts at two options and scales to four through Perk Option Quantity. First Perk Choice guarantees one selected perk as the top option on the first offer, but Auto Pick Ranking can still override it if a higher-ranked perk is also present. Auto Pick Perks then chooses the top-listed option from the final ordering rather than evaluating a separate hidden priority system.
interaction_summary: Perk labs expand the number of choices, guarantee a first perk, and control how auto-pick and ranking behave when multiple priority systems are active.

topic: Perk Wave Requirement with Standard Perk Math
title: Perk Wave Requirement with Standard Perk Math
disambiguation: This chunk is about the interaction between Perk Wave Requirement and Standard Perk Math, not the individual mechanics. It is not about perk selection order, lab completion times, or unrelated formulas.
content: Perk Wave Requirement with Standard Perk Math. Perk Wave Requirement belongs to the additive side of standard perk math. That means each copy of the perk is scaled by Standard Perk Bonus before being applied in the wave-requirement formula. The result changes the first perk timing within each base-wave bracket, and decimal outputs are floored before projecting later perk timings in the same bracket.
interaction_summary: Perk Wave Requirement is one of the additive standard perks, so its effective reduction scales with Standard Perk Bonus instead of using the multiplicative perk formula.

topic: Random Ultimate Weapon Perk with Ultimate Weapon Perks
title: Random Ultimate Weapon Perk with Ultimate Weapon Perks
disambiguation: This chunk is about the interaction between Random Ultimate Weapon Perk and Ultimate Weapon Perks, not the individual mechanics. It is not about permanent weapon ownership, labs, or unrelated random pools.
content: Random Ultimate Weapon Perk with Ultimate Weapon Perks. Random Ultimate Weapon Perk chooses a weapon the account does not already own and grants a semi-upgraded run-only version. Once that run-only weapon exists, its related Ultimate Weapon perk can enter the pool for that run. This does not unlock the permanent lab tree for that weapon, and once the account owns every weapon the random perk is removed from the pool entirely.
interaction_summary: The random ultimate weapon perk can temporarily add a weapon the player does not own, which then lets the related weapon-specific perk appear for that run.

title: Relics Overview
disambiguation: This chunk is about the Relics mechanic itself, not its interactions. It is not about event threshold relic progress, unrelated tracker state, or non-relic systems outside this mechanic.
content: Relics Overview. Relics are passive buffs that increase tower abilities. Unlocked relics apply automatically instead of requiring manual activation or equipment swaps. The themes menu is where players can view which relics have been unlocked.

title: Relic Usage and Stacking
disambiguation: This chunk is about the Relic Usage mechanic itself, not its interactions. It is not about event threshold relic progress, unrelated tracker state, or non-relic systems outside this mechanic.
content: Relic Usage and Stacking. Relic bonuses are passive and remain active automatically after the relic is unlocked. Relic bonuses are additive with similar relic bonuses. Relic bonuses are multiplicative with other bonus systems.

title: Relics Unlock Methods
disambiguation: This chunk is about the Relic Unlock Methods mechanic itself, not its interactions. It is not about event threshold relic progress, unrelated tracker state, or non-relic systems outside this mechanic.
content: Relics Unlock Methods. Relics have 6 main unlock routes. Milestone wave 4500 rewards: Some relics are unlocked from reaching wave 4500 on milestone tiers. Tournament placement: Some relics are awarded for tournament placement results. Event completion: Some relics come from event completion thresholds rather than direct shop purchases. Event rerun store purchases: Event store relics can only be obtained during event reruns. Guild store: Some relics can be bought through guild shop or guild-season relic offers. Years of gameplay: Some relics are long-term anniversary-style rewards tied to years played.

content: Relics Total Possible Bonuses. Current total possible relic bonuses are grouped into Misc, Damage, Defense, and Utility sections. The published relic totals currently cover 27 tracked stat lines: Misc 2, Damage 9, Defense 8, and Utility 8. Examples from the published totals include Lab Speed 71%, Damage 97%, Health 103%, and Coins 80%.

title: Relics with Theme Relic Menu
disambiguation: This chunk is about the interaction between Relics and Theme Relic Menu, not the individual mechanics. It is not about event thresholds, unrelated cosmetic menus, or tracker implementation details.
content: Relics with Theme Relic Menu. Relics are passive bonuses that stay active after unlock rather than sitting in a separate equip screen. Theme Relic Menu is the place where the player checks which relics are unlocked and what the cumulative relic totals currently add up to. That makes the relic system itself separate from the menu that exposes its ownership and summary information.
interaction_summary: Relics are the passive system, while Theme Relic Menu is the UI surface that shows unlocked relics and their cumulative bonuses.

topic: Relic Unlock Methods with Milestones, Tournaments, and Guild Relics
title: Relic Unlock Methods with Milestones, Tournaments, and Guild Relics
disambiguation: This chunk is about the interaction between Relic Unlock Methods, Milestones, Tournaments, and Guild Relics, not the individual mechanics. It is not about event threshold relic rewards, tracker totals, or unrelated cosmetic shops.
content: Relic Unlock Methods with Milestones, Tournaments, and Guild Relics. Relic Unlock Methods is not tied to one progression source. Milestones provide wave-4500 relic rewards, Tournaments add placement-based relic rewards, and Guild Relics adds guild-shop access to another relic acquisition path. Years-played rewards also exist outside those three systems, so relic acquisition is spread across long-term progression, competitive placement, and guild economy sources.
interaction_summary: Relic Unlock Methods pulls permanent relics from milestone wave 4500 clears, tournament placement rewards, and guild-shop relic offers.

topic: Relic Unlock Methods with Event Relic Progress and Event Relics
title: Relic Unlock Methods with Event Relic Progress and Event Relics
disambiguation: This chunk is about the interaction between Relic Unlock Methods, Event Relic Progress, and Event Relics, not the individual mechanics. It is not about tournament badges, guild offers, or unrelated medal sinks.
content: Relic Unlock Methods with Event Relic Progress and Event Relics. Relic Unlock Methods includes both event completion and event store acquisition, but those are not the same path. Event Relic Progress handles relics earned from current-event medal thresholds, while Event Relics covers the medal-shop relic offers sold through event store inventory. Because store relics only return on event reruns, event-based relic collection depends on both present-event performance and the future rerun schedule for shop availability.
interaction_summary: Relic Unlock Methods splits event-based relic access into two paths: earned threshold relics from Event Relic Progress and purchased relics from Event Relics during rerun-store availability.

title: Relic Usage with Workshop
disambiguation: This chunk is about the interaction between Relic Usage and Workshop, not the individual mechanics. It is not about relic unlock routes, tracker reminders, or unrelated progression screens.
content: Relic Usage with Workshop. Relic Usage says relic bonuses stay active automatically and stack additively with similar relic bonuses. Workshop remains the base stat-upgrade system for rows like damage, health, coins, crit factor, attack speed, and other relic-affected attributes. That means relic totals do not replace Workshop progression; they layer on top of it and multiply with other bonus systems to raise the final value further.
interaction_summary: Relic Usage adds passive relic totals on top of matching stats, while Workshop remains the underlying stat-upgrade system those bonuses amplify.

title: Tiers Overview
disambiguation: This chunk is about the Tiers mechanic itself, not its interactions. It is not about tournament brackets, tracker filters, or unrelated scaling systems.
content: Tiers Overview. Tiers are the main game difficulty ladder and currently span Tier 1 through Tier 21. Unlocking the next tier is handled through Milestones after reaching the required wave on the current tier. Tiers 2 through 15 unlock at wave 100 of the previous tier, while Tiers 16 through 21 unlock at wave 300 of the previous tier. Tier 14 and above add static battle conditions that stay fixed for the tier instead of rotating like tournament conditions. Coin bonus scaling starts at Tier 1 with 1x coins and reaches Tier 21 with 60x coins.

title: Tier Coin Bonus
disambiguation: This chunk is about the Tier Coin Bonus mechanic itself, not its interactions. It is not about tournament brackets, tracker filters, or unrelated scaling systems.
content: Tier Coin Bonus. Tier Coin Bonus is the basic reward multiplier for choosing a harder tier. Representative breakpoints are Tier 1 = 1x, Tier 5 = 4.2x, Tier 10 = 8.7x, Tier 14 = 17.6x, Tier 16 = 25.2x, Tier 21 = 60x. Higher tiers pay substantially more coins, but from Tier 14 onward that extra payout is paired with static battle conditions that permanently raise run difficulty.

title: Tier Unlock Requirement
disambiguation: This chunk is about the Tier Unlock Requirement mechanic itself, not its interactions. It is not about tournament brackets, tracker filters, or unrelated scaling systems.
content: Tier Unlock Requirement. Tier unlock requirements are based on the previous tier, and the unlocked tier is awarded through the milestone ladder rather than from an isolated tier menu. Early tier unlocks follow 100-wave clears from Tier 1 through Tier 14. Late tier unlocks shift to 300-wave clears for Tier 16 through Tier 21.

title: Battle Condition Definitions
disambiguation: This chunk is about the Battle Condition Definitions mechanic itself, not its interactions. It is not about tournament brackets, tracker filters, or unrelated scaling systems.
content: Battle Condition Definitions. Death Ray Resistance: Instead of destroying enemies, Death Ray deals a percentage of enemy health as damage. Thorns Resistance: Thorns deals a reduced percentage of its normal damage. Enemy Attack Speed: Enemy attack speed is increased by a percentage. Knockback Resistance: Knockback force applied to enemies is reduced by a percentage. Plasma Cannon Resistance: Plasma Cannon deals a reduced percentage of its normal damage. More Enemies: More enemies spawn than normal by a percentage increase. Orb Resistance: Instead of destroying enemies, orbs deal a percentage of enemy health as damage. More Bosses: Bosses spawn every set number of waves instead of every 10 waves. Enemy Speed: Enemies move faster by a percentage. Armored Enemies: Enemies block the first set number of hits they take. Energy Shields Down: Energy Shield recharge time is increased. Death Defy Down: Death Defy chance is reduced. Ultimate Weapon Durations: Chrono Field, Golden Tower, Poison Swamp, and Black Hole durations are reduced. Protector's Ultimate: Protector shields gain knockback, shockwave, and Black Hole damage immunity for a duration/cooldown profile. Tank's Ultimate: Tanks behave like bosses but stop moving once inside tower range for a duration/cooldown profile. Basic's Ultimate: Basic enemies gain a chance to spawn as other enemy types. Boss's Ultimate: Bosses spawn with overheal that boosts their health by a percentage. Ranged Ultimate: Ranged enemy projectiles disable the tower from firing for a duration. Fast's Ultimate: Fast enemies buff nearby enemies to match their speed. Scatter Ultimate: Scatter children gain increased health by a percentage. Ray Ultimate: Ray enemies fire faster by a percentage. Vampire Ultimate: Vampires drain faster by a percentage. Mass Enforcement: Surviving enemies gain mass every wave they remain alive. Skip Decay: Enemy health and attack level skip chances are reduced by a value every set number of waves. Skip Reduction - Multiply: Enemy health and attack level skip chances are multiplied by a reduction factor. Skip Reduction - Subtract: Enemy health and attack level skip chances are reduced by subtracting a flat value.

title: Tiers with Milestones
disambiguation: This chunk is about the interaction between Tiers and Milestones, not the individual mechanics. It is not about premium tracks, event difficulty, or unrelated unlock trees.
content: Tiers with Milestones. Tier progression is not a separate unlock ladder from Milestones. Instead, the account earns the next tier by reaching the required wave on the current tier, and Milestones then deliver that tier unlock reward. That requirement is usually wave 100, but it increases to wave 300 for Tier 16 through Tier 21 unlocks.
interaction_summary: Tier progression is awarded through Milestones, using wave targets on the current tier to unlock the next one.

topic: Tier Coin Bonus with Tier Battle Conditions
title: Tier Coin Bonus with Tier Battle Conditions
disambiguation: This chunk is about the interaction between Tier Coin Bonus and Tier Battle Conditions, not the individual mechanics. It is not about tournament rewards, milestone resource totals, or unrelated economy formulas.
content: Tier Coin Bonus with Tier Battle Conditions. Tier Coin Bonus rises steadily across the tier ladder, which is why later tiers are valuable for coin farming and account progression once they are stable. From Tier 14 onward, that higher payout is balanced by fixed battle conditions such as resistances, extra bosses, and enemy ultimates. In practice, each higher tier is both a reward multiplier and a difficulty profile, not just a flat coin-bonus increase.
interaction_summary: Later tiers pay more coins, but the payout increase comes with fixed battle-condition packages that sharply raise run difficulty.

title: Tournaments Overview
disambiguation: This chunk is about the Tournaments mechanic itself, not its interactions. It is not about tracker pages, unrelated event systems, or generic resource descriptions outside tournaments.
content: Tournaments Overview. Tournaments are competitive events with 30 players per bracket. The six tournament leagues are Copper, Silver, Gold, Platinum, Champion, and Legend. Primary rewards are gems and power stones, and Legend additionally rewards keys used in the Vault tech trees. Tournaments are the main recurring source of power stones for Ultimate Weapon progression. The tournament league ladder is Copper, Silver, Gold, Platinum, Champion, Legend.

title: Tournament Entry
disambiguation: This chunk is about the Tournament Entry mechanic itself, not its interactions. It is not about tracker pages, unrelated event systems, or generic resource descriptions outside tournaments.
content: Tournament Entry. Tournaments unlock at Milestones Tier 1 Wave 60. Entering a tournament run costs one tournament ticket. The highest wave reached in that run is the score used for tournament ranking and rewards. Tournaments cannot be joined while the account is already inside another active run. Tournament unlock requirement is Tier 1 Wave 60. Tournament start cadence is Wednesday 00:00 UTC and Saturday 00:00 UTC.

title: Tournament Tickets
disambiguation: This chunk is about the Tournament Tickets mechanic itself, not its interactions. It is not about tracker pages, unrelated event systems, or generic resource descriptions outside tournaments.
content: Tournament Tickets. One free ticket is granted whenever a tournament starts. Extra tickets can be earned by watching an ad or by spending gems. Gem ticket price starts at 10 gems and increases by 10 gems for each additional ticket purchased during the same tournament window. Each run costs 1 ticket, and gem repurchases scale by 10 gems each time starting from 10. Because tournament ranking uses the best wave from each purchased entry, extra tickets are a direct way to buy more attempts in the same tournament window.

title: Tournament Promotion and Demotion
disambiguation: This chunk is about the Tournament Promotion mechanic itself, not its interactions. It is not about tracker pages, unrelated event systems, or generic resource descriptions outside tournaments.
content: Tournament Promotion and Demotion. As of v25, the top four players in each league are promoted to the next league. From Platinum onward, the bottom six players are demoted to the league below. Copper and Silver are protected leagues in the sense that once they are left, the account cannot be demoted back into them. Copper: Top 4 promote to Silver. No demotion bracket is applied here. Silver: Top 4 promote to Gold. No demotion bracket is applied here. Gold: Top 4 promote to Platinum. No demotion bracket is applied here. Platinum: Top 4 promote to Champion. Ranks 25-30 demote to Gold. Champion: Top 4 promote to Legend. Ranks 25-30 demote to Platinum. Legend: No higher league exists above this one. Ranks 25-30 demote to Champion.

title: Tournament Difficulty
disambiguation: This chunk is about the Tournament Difficulty mechanic itself, not its interactions. It is not about tracker pages, unrelated event systems, or generic resource descriptions outside tournaments.
content: Tournament Difficulty. Tournament leagues use tier-plus difficulty, which scales enemy stats more aggressively than the normal tier ladder. Copper is harder than Tier 1 but easier than Tier 2, while Champion sits between Tier 11 and Tier 12 in raw stat scaling. Enemy stat growth increases across leagues for health, attack, mass, and effective movement pressure. Heat ramps up over the run and reaches maximum strength at wave 1000 for most modifiers, while More Bosses stays fixed by league. Tournament difficulty should be treated as its own scaling ladder rather than as a renamed normal tier, because league pressure changes both stat growth and battle-condition load.

title: Tournament Heat
disambiguation: This chunk is about the Tournament Heat mechanic itself, not its interactions. It is not about tracker pages, unrelated event systems, or generic resource descriptions outside tournaments.
content: Tournament Heat. Heat is active in every league above Copper and adds static plus random battle-condition pressure to tournament runs. More Bosses is always present and shortens the boss cycle by league, from every 10 waves in Copper to every 5 waves in Legend. Gold, Platinum, Champion, and Legend also guarantee an enemy level skip reduction heat at 10%, 20%, 30%, and 50% respectively. From Platinum upward, either Death Defy Down or Energy Shields Down is also active alongside the league-specific random conditions. Copper: no random heat package, and bosses spawn every 10 waves. Silver: bosses spawn every 9 waves and 1 random battle condition are added. Gold: bosses spawn every 8 waves and 2 random battle conditions are added. Guaranteed heat: Enemy Level Skip Reduction 10%. Platinum: bosses spawn every 7 waves and 3 random battle conditions are added. Guaranteed heat: Enemy Level Skip Reduction 20%, Death Defy Down or Energy Shields Down. Champion: bosses spawn every 6 waves and 4 random battle conditions are added. Guaranteed heat: Enemy Level Skip Reduction 30%, Death Defy Down or Energy Shields Down. Legend: bosses spawn every 5 waves and 5 random battle conditions are added. Guaranteed heat: Enemy Level Skip Reduction 50%, Death Defy Down or Energy Shields Down.
